Very political process in getting promoted... more about who you know and who you can get to recognize you than what you accomplish.  Lots of middle managers more focused on how things are perceived to upper management rather than getting things done.  I saw deliveries that were ready to go being held back so that upper management wouldn't be expecting fast deliveries all the time or to keep from someone higher up the chain from looking good... as I said, very political.

summary: Something never changes at DB.  Now DOJ is looking into... STAY AWAY AS MANY HAVE SAID
advice: Listen to your people.  They have good ideas and stop your managers who are full of attitudes and think they can get away with anything.  They insult people, but they don't bring anything good to the table.  They reject qualified people we recommend onboard because they want to protect their clan and don't want anyone to challenge their authority.  We lost so many good candidates not because they were unqualified because they would challenge the status quo of the existing managers.  The managers feel the new candidates will not do what they want them to, so they reject well-qualified candidates.  Hopefully, such negative publicity will get you to act.
pros: There can't be any because the US Department of Justice (MAY) look into this bank.
cons: Where to start because they never seem to listen and pay attention to what their people tell them. Change the attitude and behavior of your middle managers. They need an agency like the DOJ to say to them or get a headline in WSJ that DOJ may look into them to get them to change their ways

summary: A great exercise in what NOT to do.
advice: Start taking a look at the REAL reason your employees leave.  Exit interviews should mandatory and the data taken seriously.  When an entire department leaves in 5 months, look at the MD of that department.  Not only does he not know what he’s doing and goes to the gym for two hours in the middle the day, but he never spends time with his team or one on one to know what they are doing.  Isn’t that what managers are supposed to do?  Instead, he kisses everyone’s behind, so you think he’s wonderful.  Think again.
pros:
Pay
Benefits
Perks
Hours
Cafeteria
401k match 
I can’t think of anything else.
cons:
Upper management has no idea as to what their MDs are doing, and don’t care when you bring it to their attention.
Pass the buck and blame others culture.
Parent company in Germany does not care about regulatory implications and how it affects the US.
When you bring an idea to management for improvement, it’s shut down.

advice: Lower and middle management need to promote from within. Too often, management accepts unrealistic expectations of senior management because they don't know what work is possible.
pros: Generous benefits and leave time. Decent pay if you are coming in off the street. COVID work from home is nice which may be the future. Even when in the office, lunches, breaks, and clock-in/clock-outs are not micromanaged unless you abuse them.
cons: Promotions are political, only once a year, and you are often passed over. You are expected to perform the role of your promotion without its pay while you compete to be promoted. Often times, despite your efforts, you are passed over. Better luck next year. In middle and back office, annual pay increase is weak, so you may likely not get paid what the new hire you train gets paid.

advice: share information a bit more
pros: i think db is generally a good place to work because the people are nice, good environment and generally a lot of opportunities for growth. Because db is a global company the opportunities for travel is enormous. Many of my colleagues have traveled to Moscow, London, Frankfurt, Sydney and Tokyo. I think compared to its pairs db is truly a global company. The internal training is good as well. There are a lot of classes available to develop your personal brand etc. DB is growing int he US and I think it creates many opportunities to be apart of something big.
cons: Sometimes in large organizations like this it can be way too bureaucratic. I think there is too much levels and roles, that creates and overly complex environment.

pros:
Salary is good
Wfh us good
Leaves great
Cabs
Time
cons: Loads of work in the bank

summary: Employer of last resort. Consider another industry.
advice: Evolve. Mature. Talent will come back and this once great firm could be great again.
pros: Exposure to many smart people. Fast computer. Good work from home flexibility. The time off policy, if you can use it, is generous. The resume line is nice too, for now. Very smart people are attracted to the DB brand so you get to work with them for a few months or a year or two before they leave, or until you do.
cons: Soft compensation. Tough industry. Unsustainable employment strategy. Lack of strategic direction. Ineffective HR. Lack of expertise: blind leading the blind. Confrontational behaviors, occasional bullying due to competitive rating system. (quiet people with alot of talent but who aren't aggressive don't really get much justice out of the bell curve rating scale) Promotions get held up due to HR not knowing what they are doing. Good people getting burned up. Napoleonic politics. Weak training. Long arbitrary hours and not due to actual needs, but usually due to bureaucracy and inefficiency. Weak technology implementation and SDLC.

advice: Instead of always trying to define global standards and initiatives’, that never seem to make it into production (or at least they take a very long time), give regions some autonym to make more decisions. This would enable them to meet the needs of the local business requirements.
pros: The organization follows the European attitudes towards work life balance. Time off and flexible work schedules are usually not a problem. Most of the people are great to deal with.
cons:
Compensation is below market rate (at least in IT). Additionally, they are aggressively looking to outsource/off shore any thing they possible can. This leads to very poor moral and a feeling of just trying to get by day-to-day. 

For IT, the center of the universe is London, then Frankfurt, and finally NY. Get use to it.

advice: Take a look at what you've got - invest in them so you don't have a high turnover and you'll wind up with some loyal, hard working devoted employees.. Keep treating us the way you do and nothing will change  - you'll spend a lot more training new people who are only going to quit in a short period of time anyway.
pros: Compensation is ok.. People are nice and hard working for the most part.  DB may be a good way to get your foot into the Investment banking world, but DB isn't a place that you will likely stay.
cons: Management / opportunities for advancement are minimal.  Management is only looking out for themselves - which happens elsewhere too but DB Mgmt is not wise enough to see that treating employees well will pay off by getting loyal, hard working people.  Instead, it's typical to use someone up, and they'll quit.  Then Mgmt has to train someone else to do the job.   Advancement is basically nill - you can only really advance if someone higher than you quits (which does happen fairly often but even so, you aren't guarenteed a promotion - even if you deserve it and are very capable of performing the position.

summary: Decent place like any other sell side bank
advice:
Please don't overpay to front office staff.  Its outrageous how much greed is there. Let people come to work for db to make a difference and have sustainable profit. Cut the MDs and Ds you have in infrastructure and reduce your cost footprint.
Eliminate the director title like Goldman and have VPs become partners or get equity upside. This will drastically change the bottom line in 2 years and DB will be the number 1 place to work
pros: If you are in infrastructure  roles like IT, Finance, Risk - then work life is good. Paid leave of 5 weeks + 2 personal days and sick days. Colleagues are friendly and there is a good social network around you. Base compensation and benefits are above par ( meaning they will beat  JPM, MS etc for most new hires). Internal mobility in some teams is good.
cons: Lack of compensation and growth once you lock yourself inn. This leads to frustration and lack of engagement amongst people who have been on job for say 4 or more years. Lousy systems and very slow decision making by management. Heavy push to move more jobs to India from the investment bank ( and just me the 24hr time difference doesn't work well when resolving issues)

summary: It was a good company to work for. . .
advice: C'mon guys, 52% increment for yourselves, but leave the staff year after year after year with no increments? That is leadership.
pros: You can learn to navigate a snake pit. Also, could potentially learn to avoid being eaten by piranhas.
cons: Well, the only time that you will get a raise is if you are promoted. The problem is that promotions are incredibly difficult to secure. The easier way to get promoted at DB is to get a job at another company, then come back a year later at a higher corporate rank. There is no governance process for the hiring at a given corporate rank, but if you seek a promotion within the organization, tons and tons of hurdles to overcome. Good luck.

pros:
Food, salary and all, 
,.....
.....
....
...
cons: Good salary good colleagues everything good no cons.

jobTitle: Manager- Midlevel (Associate to Assistant Vice President)
advice: Turn things upside down and start over. Old way of management is both ineffective and demoralizing.
pros: New CEO hopefully can turn things around.
cons: Poor management structure. Upper management is not close to the ground. Review process is obsolete and can be bias at times. Matrix management set-up is inefficient, upper management is more concerned about the bottom line than people (e.g. push back on a 1K increase for new hire). Many promises to deliver change but limited to no tangible results. Senior managers lack people development skills and are largely SME's promoted to positions based upon task knowledge and not key leadership attributes. During the review process, managers miss the big picture and tend to focus on 1-2 small mistakes instead of the year at hand all while overlooking their lack of leadership and involvement.

jobTitle: Assistant Vice President - Global Capital Markets
summary: Too big and the technology is really outdated
advice: Spend the money to improve our technology.  DB has double the headcount of other banks to do the same work because everyone is doing things in excel manually which is not fulfilling and drives good people away while the zombies stay forever.  Streamline the bank.  We need serious management consulting advice to make the bank more productive.
pros:
Truly global bank, diversity
Socially responsible firm that sponsors charities and the arts
Strong balance sheet so jobs are safe in this tough environment
Some great people to work with from all over the world
Pretty laid back atmosphere compared to other investment banks
Easy to get promoted/fast tracked if you work hard, not psycho competitive like other banks, but requires quite a bit of ass kissing
cons:
Technology is very old
Lots of manual processes, very little automation
Extremely political, not a real meritocracy at all
Very slow to make decisions
Tons of red tape:  need all kinds of sign-offs to do even simple/unimportant things
Tons of redundency and segregation of duties makes it hard to get anything done because no one "owns" anything

summary: Easy on career, better work-life balance
advice:
Understand the impact of strategy to the people and business:
ex: Moving jobs from London and NJ to Cary - and then hiring people in Cary to report to managers in NJ and London - caused complete disharmony and a conflict of interest among teams. This impacted deliveries across the board.

Too many vendors - Lead to lack of accountability and the piecing together of ridiculous SLAs across all teams.
pros:
DBGT has great benefits packages, reasonable pay packages. 
The team I worked with in Cary was great.

Work hours were relatively manageable.
cons:
There are not enough resources for self learning. Very few CBTs available.
Relatively few trainings held in classroom as well, other than the ones pushed down from management.
DBGT is a separate legal entity - meant for software development for the bank. Downside, it got disconnected from the business and employees lack exposure to business knowledge and requirements, yet the organisation as a whole is just as regulated as the business, coz its still a bank. Makes it extremely hard to actually work and get ahead in your career. I have tried networking extremely well across the organisation, but DBGT has too many strategic issues, leading to a lot of internal politics to fight against, to get anything done.

advice: There have been a lot of cultural overhauls to DB (and other top banks) but still not a great place to work for junior staff. The handling of bonuses for VP's in 2016 dealt a big blow to the morale for junior staff.
pros:
-Brand recognition (especially in Europe and Asia, not so much in the US recently because of the recent negative headlines)
-People are pretty nice compared to other IB's in SF; not as many egos
-Location (beats working in the South Bay)
-Very strong semiconductor practice (other verticals, not so much)
cons:
Aside from the typical cons of working in IB as a junior banker (such as long, unpredictable hours):
-Deal flow was lacking; possibly due to a lot of negative headlines in 2016-2017
-Infrastructure/technology is laughable. No such thing as collaborative software (i.e. Google docs)

advice: In my years there, I saw little employee loyalty to the company. Just loyalty to the money. I worked in Global Markets. I went from "you're a star" to "we are now doing this in Bangelore" very quickly. Perhaps more consideration could be given to the human capital at DB.
pros: Great pay, benefits. If you do your job, they treat you well.
cons: If you happen to be in an area that is affected by outsourcing (and many of the largest areas were), you should look to work somewhere else. They will not consider strong performers in one area as potentially strong performers in another. Moving around in the company is available to the very few. No matter how well you do in a support function, if "the numbers" don't work for you, you are out. Great to be a stockholder, though. I still have all of my shares. Review process was great financially, terrible professionally (in terms of advancement). They expect you to do your job, and don't consider the fact that you could do something else, something more challenging.

pros: Lack of internal competition, because quality is so poor
cons: Worst work culture I have ever experienced

advice: Jacksonville management doesn't think for themselves they only follow marching orders from NY.  So any advice would be pointless
pros:
Regardless of your level of experience in excel your skills will dramatically improve.

Endless coffee
cons:
Beware of any  positions with Reporting in the description or title.  These are old school "sweat shop" positions.

They will tell you that you may have to work more then 40 hours a week in the interview, but in reality you will be expected to work 60-to 80 hours a week including weekends.

You will most likely not be able to take a vacation because we were told that we would need three back-ups for our processes before an approval would be considered.  The turn-over is so high there is no chance of training three back ups. Zero family life balance.

Work is 99% excel driven data mining and data entry.  

If you can see your self sitting behind a computer doing data entry for 10 to 12 hours a day, never seeing the daylight and not being able to take a vacation - this jobs for you.

It is rumored that other departments are better - you will not be able to post for them for at least 2 years (If nothing has changed)

advice:
look at your values: 
# Performance
We are committed to a result-oriented culture.
# Trust
We behave reliably, fairly and honestly.
# Teamwork
We benefit from the diversity of our business and our people by working together to achieve success.
# Innovation
We are constantly challenging conventional wisdom and developing new solutions to meet customer requirements.
# Client Focus
We place customers at the centre of our activities and they drive all that we do.

Integrity is not on the list. And it shows. It takes a lot of performance, teamwork, inovation and client focus to build Trust without Integrity. But it's much harder to maintain it.
pros:
Smart and ambitious people. Unfortunately it's either or...
Great Training for soft skills , finance and technology. Top notch graduate program.
Excellent benefits. Competitive salaries. Above avarage vacation days.
cons: Unreasonably long hours. The place is a Sweatshop.

summary: Steer clear! Bank has major issues
advice: Get rid of the Managing Directors that do nothing but sit in their office while those below do all the work and then the MDs take all of the credit. Most MDs add no value but cost big bucks. Figure out a strategy and stick with it!
pros: vacation, other benefits and mostly good people.
cons: Where to start! There is a reason that DB is always in the news and that’s because risk, audit, legal and compliance departments have sub-par employees. Legal won’t make a decision on anything and always has to go to outside counsel for something that the in-house counsel should know Management in Germany and London don’t care about US regulations. You can literally tell management that you will have a regulatory problem yet they ignore any pleas for help. No ownership at the senior level! No one can make a decision so nothing gets done which results in those that want to see progress give up eventually and leave.

pros: good team, great to work
cons: less pay, that's all mostly

summary: Deutsche Bank is a very good company to work for.
advice: Be more specific about the future vision for the bank so employees know what to pay most attention too.
pros: Deutsche bank has very flexible working schedules for working Moms including on-sight day care in time of emergency. Great benefits including healthcare, matching 401K, pension benefits, 4 week minimum vacation.
cons: Frequent policy changes and restructuring and at times you'll be working towards a goal that is no longer a priority. We were told the bank is committed to a 25% ROI (Return on Equity) year over year which makes cost cutting a number one priority,  but recently found out that the goal was considered unrealistic and we should focus on providing quality. Slow steady growth with quality is now the main goal.

advice:
- Better internal HR website to make openings within the bank more transparent and to promote movement internally
- Make 360 feedback (staff rate their managers) mandatory. The most common reason people leave their position is because of their manager
pros:
- Advancement is based on meritocracy.
- Benefits are among the best of it's competitors.
- Compensation is based on performance. High performers are paid well. Low performers are not.
cons:
- The internal HR recruiting is not great which makes moving between different groups at DB dependent on individuals but this has improved over the past couple of years
- Promotions can be very political as committees comprised of senior managers outside of evaluatee's organization are part of the process

advice: Top level down reorganization would be a good idea. Middle managers need to help their people advance, not encourage stagnation.  Some directors are NOT qualified to be directors.
pros: Brilliant group of people, strong culture and diversity. Mostly everyone had an mba, phD, licenses. Lots of intellectual capital there. 20 vacation days. Small relocation bonus. Some opportunity for working remotely.
cons:
What good are all those days if you can never take them?
They promise 20% bonuses to entice you to relocate there, since there is next to NO talent in Jacksonville.  Then you get a 3% bonus. Don't fall for it.
Disorganized management at the upper levels. No opportunity for advancement. Bosses are indifferent to your efforts. No adequate direction in how to do your job so your efforts are wasted when you do your job and bosses make you start all over due to a new rule. Lots of politics and some annoyingly nosy team members. LOTS of turnover be it doesn't take long for the smarter people to realize morale sucks and leave.

summary: Can be good, but you need to be careful
advice: There is a lot of mistrust of management.   They know this, and have instituted Town Halls and other forms of communications, but it doesn't seem to hold. The most honest thing I heard in my tenure was "the next couple of years will be bad", but I never was convinced that a proper plan was in place to make the time afterwards better.   Management is in a hard spot, DB's capital is low, income is down and there is no clear path on how to make things better (other than "let's do what Goldman is doing").
pros: Great benefits.  The bank wants people to be happy and productive and tries through many initiatives.  A lot of smart people, but motivation is low. Good work is rewarded.
cons: Very politcal, need to step carefully.  The systems are terrible and the proposed solutions are so large that they end up failing.  Long term goals are routinely overruled by new initiatives from senior management.  There's a lot of talk about communication and making things better for employees, but cost cutting and new regulations routinely trump those initiaves.  It can be hard to make meaningful changes from the trenches.

summary: DB America good, DB Germany bad
advice: German management should embrace professionalism rather than sandbagging their own position with our mediocre people around them.
pros: US investment bank colleagues are excellent and it has good leadership and culture. Great building in NY. Friendly and collaborative culture within the US.
cons:
The retail bank totally sucks and drags the rest of the bank down with it. There is a discount on what you can earn due to the IB bailing out the broken parts of the bank which they don't even want to fix as it is too political.

The IT is a horror show and there is no sign of them improving it (except for the IB platforms of course, which are strong).

Many (not all) German colleagues are often appointed due to their nationality and would never merit their role if it were a real meritocracy. The have no idea how bad they are, as Germany has no successful banks so in their context DB is the top of the mountain, but in reality, it is a very small mole hill when compared with US banks.

summary: Software mass-production factory for Deutsche Bank in Moscow
advice: Move towards flat org structure; pay more attention to your staff and less to political games; start to recognize and reward the talent inside the company.
pros:
- Some of IT projects are engineerengly challenging and widely used in the bank
- competitive salary, especially for higher ranks
- good and nice colleagues
- flexible working hours
- the company has started to spend a lot on IT, especially in recent years
- job security, you can successfully pretend to be working for years
- flexible working hours
- business class transcontinental flights
cons:
- Inefficient management obsessed with maintaining good relations with their bosses no matter what and keeping the status quo
- highly hierarchical management structure with many levels of hierarchy and employees on all levels being supposed to "know their places"
- favoritism and lack of promotion and recognition for the rest
- innovation culture is not there at all, you do what you're told to do and keep your ideas to yourself unless someone higher than you has expressed them already
- no perks, goodies and amenities
- crappy office (this will change in 2011 when they move to a different building)
- high workload on some projects
- overbureacratic and very slow internal processes, like buying the software that you need to do the job, etc.

summary: Only work here (specifically in Cary) if you have no other option left in life
advice:
Everyone understands that the company is going through rough time, but the least you can do is to treat people nicely. 

Cary location needs some change badly and all the reviews that you read cannot be wrong.  Start by changing HR managers (they screw up people more than helping them and treat them just like numbers). Not even a basic exit interview of employees is practised here.
pros: Chill work-life (10-4 kind of job); Generally, people are nice to talk to; active engagement groups
cons:
Every little process is broken (you will experience it in the initial onboarding process itself); worst HR people that you can work with; God bless if you are on a work/ student visa because HR messed up with so many of my international coworkers over these 5 years.

Management (especially Directors) in Cary location have no clue about work. I have seen a few directors who are given the team just for approving absence requests. Some of them work as moral guards whose only job is to make sure people are coming on time and dressing up properly (know one director who commented on someone's attire multiple times)

summary: Good start for career, but Deutsche Bank needs to do a lot better
advice:
In one short phrase, management lacks vision.

Examples:

A.  Sometime in 2005-2006, addressing a large crowd of interns / graduate training full-hires, one of the current co-CEOs emphasizes: "Great banks need three things: (a) market access, (b) intellectual property, (c) prop trading.  We have (a) and (b), but are behind industry leader (Goldman) in (c).

Same person in 2009: "Prop has no business inside a broker-dealer investment bank".

B.  Circa 2005-2006, top US-based economist, to a large crowd of newly minted employees: "There is no housing bubble in the USA.  In fact, I just closed on my house",

C.  Circa 2008, top US-based government affairs economist to a large crowd of trainees: "The US Government will not allow GM to fail; therefore, I am buying GM common stock".  Needless to say, 

D.  Co-CEO, circa 2012: "We don't need to raise capital.".  Well, we all know what happened.
pros:
- Great graduate training program
- Excellent market access
- Excellent analytics
- Some excellent areas work in, but difficult to identify
- Great (not excellent) benefits
- Excellent training opportunities
cons:
- Poor technology platform, even by bank standards
- Attrition too high
- Too much politics
- Too much wasted resources
- Top management (esp CEO) not visioinary

advice: Please look into processes, there are many flaws, no one cares internally as people are with bank from decades, and they are sure no one can touch them.
pros:
* Sufficient leaves
* WFH
* Work life balance
* If you are lucky, you can get a good manager
cons:
This list is not going to end for sure
* After working for 2.5 yrs you expect smooth exit, but HR is like wait Hold my beer, What is the process again?
* After leaving the bank, I received my full salary for the last month (includes 7 days extra pay), had to call my manager and inform about this and get the thing sorted.
* After 10 days asked them where is my experience certificate, HR team says we just came to know 10 days ago you are leaving, it will take another 10 days, Wow process said someone.
* HR is just a lazy guy, eats money and does nothing.
* Want to work here, go ahead on your own risk, communication team consist of many saints, and hope you never have anything to do with them.
* Are you someone who is interested to speak an conferences, even if its for open source, look away this is not the organization you want to work for.

pros:
good pay
upward mobility 
Fun
cons: Not a great amount of coworkers

advice: Right now DB is talking a lot about how to "fix" itself. But DB's vision going forward is unclear beyond upgrading its financial ratios. Clarify what DB will be over the long-term rather than only reacting to news articles.
pros: The people were great, but we were all stressed recently. Lots of options to move internally if you are proactive and work hard. Like any large organization, understanding how to get things done and knowing who is who is a major element of success. I had several great bosses and colleagues, we made it through many challenges as a team. I consider them great friends, period.
cons: The company itself is going through major changes still remaining from the 2007-2008 financial crisis. Some business units and departments will thrive, and others will shrink. Do you own homework to evaluate the opportunity for yourself.

advice: Let people do their jobs and keep an eye out for some management elements that are not working to enhance the value of the bank or to groom talent into advancement.
pros:
Some good people interested in the well being of the bank and its products. I think the bank is a good starting platform for anyone. It has a good reputation.
Good work life balance and reasonable mobility 
Benefits are just ok, not great. They offer a lot of benefits, but on the low end of the scale.
cons:
Lots of people interested in self promotion and stardom. Sabotaging your projects and going behind one's back is not uncommon. Some leads hide behind the phrase "team effort" or "team" to avoid giving well deserved individual credit. Most important decisions are made in London or NY, leaving only low level autonomy to Cary.
No raises or bonuses in the two years I spent there.

advice: Measure twice, cut once.
pros: Various areas of the Bank you can work in.  Relatively easy to move laterally if you do well.  I worked with a lot of good people in various areas.  I would give the company a solid 3 stars here but the reason for the 2 stars is in the Cons.
cons:
Hard to be promoted.  You can be promoted in theory- i.e. start the job, be successful in the job, but formal promotions and raises take place only once a year.  So be careful.  If you get 
"promoted " in March, you will most likely not get the title or pay until perhaps February of the following year.  My advice is only take a promotion during the promoting month because at the end of the day you may never get the promotion or pay promised.  I saw this happen to several colleagues which I feel is totally unethical.

advice: Create better role definitions, and share the executive ownership across all locations.
pros: The people try very hard to make it work.  The community groups are good to get people engaged.  Overall the people create a good environment.  I learned a lot there.   Cloud adoption is a focus, so get in on the ground floor there for learning about this.   Not a bad place to get your feet wet and start a career.  Agile methods are attempted, again a good place to get started.   Benefits are very good, and pay is above average.
cons:
The executive team is in London.  It is possible to  get noticed, but it is harder with them all being remote.  Promotions above a certain level are limited outside of the main location.  

Collaborative tooling is limited, making it a challenge to work with remote team members.

summary: DB doing better than most of its peers at this point, but is that saying much?
advice: The company's fair weathering of the credit and recessionary events currently underway (as compared relative to its peers) must be acknowledged as 99% blind luck / 1% skill. Bottom line: don't rest on your laurels since they're illusory to begin with.
pros: Deutsche Bank is an investment bank (as well as commercial in non-US regions) of rising global / local reputation and clout. As a result, employee quality will hopefully rise over time.
cons: Business units are independent, hardened silos with little cross pollination of ideas and/or services that could be exploited for greater corporate gain. This is due to the highly political and territorial nature of businesses whose management were headhunted from other top tier banks (or integrated via acquisition) and are therefore deeply distrustful of the motives of colleagues whom they perceive as political adversaries contesting for the same pot of gold.

summary: Working as Product Controller in Manila Service Center
advice: With the level of attrition, Im sure the managment knows what's wrong. In all fairness, I think th top management has the best interest for the company. Just do something with the middle management and their "favoritism". It demoralizes people.
pros:
- good pay compared to other local companies
- nice office and facilities
- lots of available trainings
- can get to travel for "free"
cons:
- promotion is flawed. no clear cut qualifications how you'll be promoted. 
- have to be friends with senior bosses to be recognized otherwise you will get nowhere
- no definite career path. this is definitely just a job. growth means = complicatd products = more working hours 
- to many expats justifying their presence. too many "projects" they wanna do which of course means more admin work. 
- just one of of the resources
- politics
- miserable non-monetary benefits that you can take home and share with your family

summary: A good bank with some compromise
advice: Get off your high horses and look at how much value the organization, at any level, produce for the Bank. Reward in different ways their results and the way they achieve them with so many resources constraints (at least in the investment banking side). Recognize more the job done with global impacts by people located not only in UK, US or HK. Promote more the "diversity" with real actions and not only with nice words or events. Talk more to people about your (or given) plans and share the top management view.
pros: They promote accountability and rely a lot on personal willingness. People passionate to the banking and financial environment can find here a very good place to enhance their performances and meet their goals.
cons: All the cons linked to a big/global bank: bureaucracy, inefficiencies, lack and waste of resources that, a different level, have an impact on your job and plans.

summary: Good for lateral moves and travel. Not good for growth.
advice: Operations should be seamless entry to front office. Pay operations more and make back office able to move and learn front office. Loss of talent and the weak technology platforms is why DB is not Goldman Sachs.
pros: Some good some bad managers. The young teams are most fun. Work hard play hard. Pay is not the best but still sufficient and usually bonus is 10-30% based on bonus.
cons: The HR process and politics are real. To get a raise it is not the manager's decision but the HR department. They do not know how much you are putting in and spread the wealth according to company needs not department needs. Lateral moves are easy and moving to a different location is usually do-able but moving up might come down to having someone leave before the position opens. Jobs are very siloed, so cross training is limited therefore limiting growth opportunities.

advice: Watch the empire builders and work at streamlining the production deployment process.  There are a lot of great technologies being used, but not often a clear path as to how to use them in your environment.  Wikis exist, but they are too spread out to be of much use.  This needs to be integrated into the company's internal social networking tool.
pros: This organization is dedicated to leveraging superior technical talent to build next-generation applications for the bank.  They are willing to take the time to make the right design decisions and take the longer view of building applications across silos to decrease long-term costs.
cons: Navigating the bureaucracy to get anything done, especially as it relates to even the simplest modifications to production systems is very painful.  Organizational politics and power grabs are a bit ruthless for my taste.

advice: HR should work with responsibility. If they are not working properly higher management should keep an eye on them or else they will lose name in market.
pros: I haven't been in company for single day as HR didn't completed his formalities from his side.
cons:
Will tell you whole story and then you find out the cons. I got selected and got sufficient hike. HR forced me to resign and buy out the notice period as the requirement was at earliest. So I did the same as HR told me. Now, Before 2 days of joining date I asked him what documents need to carried at the time of joining, on which he said we need more documents without which your joining can not happen. 
Here there was no HR initiative as it was his work where as on top of that he was asking me the document at the time of joining. And without document your joining wont happen. I was shocked and surprised. I asked them why you didn't intimated it before. 
Don't trust HR of this company.

summary: Boring, bad management and terrible WFH conditions
advice: Pay for home office equipment and support us working from home. Give us a break, we have all worked so hard and there has been no real acknowledgment of it.
pros: Free vhi health insurance benefit
cons: Poor management. Managers who think the best way to do something is the way it has always been done. Don't take any feedback on board regarding processes and procedures. Upper management is so out of touch with their terrible communications. Highlighting their minor inconveniences of lockdown from their massive houses. Expecting people to work just as hard from home but without any support towards buying home office equipment or borrowing even a screen or a chair from the office. Something that every other company has done at this point. Awful KPIs which means you are micromanaged constantly. Always monitored and every minute of the day nearly has to be accounted for. Fired loads of people last year and never acknowldged it.

advice: I think separating variable compensation for AVP and below vs VP doesnt produce harder working individuals at lower levels. The recognition awards are ok, but more seen as a token, not necessarily earned by achievements, but more of making sure everyone gets a fair go. Thisis coming from a senior AVP. Also, the fact that in the new system AVPs and below, creating SMART goals are optional, is I think a mistake and a bit patronising
pros: Your team does not hinder your promotion progress i.e. there is not limit to how many AVPs, VPs can be in a team. Everyone can get promoted if they out perform the other candidates on their level across the bank. They have invested in me to travel and work in a different country at my request
cons: Its a very large bank so getting these done can be draining and some processes are quite archaic.  Focus on career progression can rely heavily on the manager you have

advice:
Be aware of how the decisions you make affect the people who have to react to them. You are relying on a small number of people who are willing to battle the bureaucracy and do all the heavy lifting to keep the show going.

The new bonus structure does not adequately reward or encourage high performance.
pros: Cary location is very friendly, good working hours most of the time, reasonably competitive salary, good vacation allowance, some opportunities for travel
cons:
Takes longer to release software than write it. Technology-wise DB is about 5 years behind the competition. Limited opportunities for upward mobility and limited autonomy. All key decisions are made in the London and New York hubs. Very little training provided, very easy to become stuck/trapped in a role.

Infrastructure support is a joke, all support is outsourced and the teams have no accountability and it shows in the level of service they provide.

summary: Great way to get an initial foot in the door
advice:
-Follow through with strategies rather than changing them. 

-Focus on employee development and give them more chances to advance up the ladder 

-Reorganize teams and focus on efficiency
pros:
-Great work/life balance (depending on department) 

-Intelligent coworkers 

-Decent access to events and company sponsored groups. 

-Laid back office culture  

-Excellent benefits
 
-A recent college grad should absolutely apply, it is a great opportunity to get some professional experience
cons:
-Ineffective upper management 

-Major bureaucracy(Objectives are not achieved)

-Company strategy seems to change every 6 months.(Leads to a severe lack of ability to follow through and lack of vision)

- Very difficult to move up the ladder (If you want to be promoted it's best to work somewhere else and come back as a re-hire)

- Positions constantly being off-shored

- Employee morale very low

- No work/life balance(depending on department, some teams work day in and day out 9 am-11 pm)

- Management not focused on developing employees  

- Easy to get pigeonholed

summary: DB tech center - a place where you can grow, but learn patience to deal with bureaucracy
advice: Try to clarify the overall IT objectives so that goals are clear on short and medium term.
pros:
- Great team spirit in the projects I worked in
- Helpful and nice colleagues of all ages  (medium age is around 30)
- In crisis situations (on the projects I am working on) management provides all support needed to unblock them 
- Support for learning and development
- A place where to further develop management and negotiation skills
cons:
- A fair share of bureaucracy - but it is expected for a bank of such calibre
- Old processes that are changing slowly (but at least people are trying to change them) - again to be expected for such a large bank
- Unclear delineation between internal and external employees - who should take ownership of what - although the overall company mission is to internalize IT skills for the time being
- Unclear IT repatriation strategy

summary: Overall a good place to work
advice: More open communication between management and their subordinates would be helpful. It is much easier to do one's job well if one knows what is expected of them and what the plans are for the future.
pros: A large population of employees some of whom have a wealth of experience and have been with the bank for a long period as well as plenty of young and dynamic people with fresh ideas. Because it is an international bank that services clients in Europe and Latin America, its employees reflect that ethnic diversity. It is also pretty easy to make connections with others in different groups and departments, which makes learning about the bank and new opportunities much easier.
cons: My team was a fairly new one so there was a lack of existing infrastructure for its management and development. Because of that, the grounds were shifting and expectations fluctuated in ways that made it difficult to anticipate what was expected of us.

advice:
-- Change people by taking constant feedback from Managers. People learned how to survive in DB without doing their work. 
-- Fire all FA's here, They are absolutely waste of money in Cary. Hire more engineers instead to get work done.
pros:
-- Good Place to play politics and Survive
-- Get here to learn how to survive without work by playing politics.
cons:
--Everything is in control of London. Cary is just an service based offshore location, People here on H1b are treated as Slaves. Node your head of what London Say. Otherwise get ready to be fired.
--There is a reason why Deutsche bank had Bad reputation in Market. Here is the Answer : People who works here
--Come here to get frustrated easily without knowing what you are coding and how is it useful to bank. Zero learning curve.
--Terrible People. People play lot of politics in own team to survive.
--No Clear requirements of what they want, but still you need to get product delivered or get ready to be blamed.
-- No one is interested to listen to Team concerns. Management feel offended if you do that.

advice: No advice. Such purblind managers can work only in such unmodern company. Continue doing it until all your employees run away
pros:
- Good salary when you start working
- Good engineers - you can improve your tech skills here.
cons:
- The most stressful environment ever. You get the salary that is 20% and then work as 2 engineers. 
- You never hear "thank you" or "good job"
- 80% of engineers never increase their salary
- only 10-15% of engineers get the annual bonus - usually that means they are b*tches or genius
- performance review process kills your mood and motivation. The only thing you should do to make carrier in DB is so-called visibility - that means more meetings, more calls, more criticizing of you colleges - just don't spend your time for coding. That is useless. 
- no HR department - that means nobody cares about your satisfaction.
- no sport compensation, no trips, no cookies, no corporate events

summary: Top quality work without the staggering burden of super-egos.
advice: Communication about overall company health (both successes and failures) is becoming increasingly important -- before it turns up in the press.  The bank should also be more aggressive in trumpeting some of it's more recent successes post-Lehman, to qualify the inevitably dreary earnings reports that all banks have and will be issuing in the near future.
pros: Tremendous opportunities for international postings and development of a global focus.  Ego tripping strongly dis-incentivized. The company is more proactive in evaluating employee strenghts/interests and seeking out opportunities for development and that perfect next assignment.
cons: Compensation structure and progression strangely rigid. The technology products can be somewhat outmoded, but are getting better. This may seem like a strange personal prejudice, but it's my contention that any organization that stubbornly refuses to move away from using Lotus Notes will never be the best at whatever it does -- we all have our litmus tests, I suppose.

summary: Deutsche Bank - a good place to acquire skills for use at another company!
advice: Empower your employees.   Take more responsibility for your criminal actions of the past.
pros:
- tuition reimbursement
- tons of pto
- looks good on resume
- inexpensive health care 
- overall excellent benefits package
- a good place to gain experience for use at other companies
cons:
- miles of red tape 
- management does not trust employees - they literally have to know where you are and what you are doing at all times.  I witnessed managers looking through cracks in bathroom stalls to find a person.  They keep files with records of when employees come and go throughout the day.
- DB does not empower it's employees - they don't trust their people to get the job done without extreme micromanagement.  
- management seems incapable of making effective, timely,  decisions.  
- dated, 30 year old systems supported by inept IT support (tata consulting)
- Deutsche Bank was involved with the Nazi's 
- inconsistent review procedures and expectations 
- if you are not tight with your boss you will go nowhere - they will promote from outside.

pros: It can be a means to an end, but not to the level of other bulge bracket investment banking platforms
cons:
The franchise is completely unstable, and has degraded over the last few years.  You will not even get a meaningful investment banking experience due to senior turnover in the last few years in core verticals (Healthcare / TMT), ongoing litigation concerns, and an inability to compete or attract talent.  Your seat is absolutely not guaranteed.

You WILL be expected to work investment banking hours with an investment banking attitude.  You will work for unambitious, incompetent managers that have no genuine care for your development (or sanity).  The stock's not undervalued; it's just actually that crappy of a platform.  I wish you the best of luck if you commit to DB, because you will certainly need it.    

Cons (bulleted):
- Bureaucracy and face time
- Horrible hours that are detrimental to mental and physical health
- Incompetence and lack of leadership at mid level (Associate & VP) 
- No meaningful deal flow or professional development
- Massive turnover and layoffs at all levels (incl. junior levels)

summary: No thinking, just give me a result!
advice: Setup working processes. Really working. Start to manage people, not just tasks. Start to manage managers, do they really do their job on managing subordinates right? Pay attention to hiring more skilled engineers and to educate juniors. Get rid of vendors in all IT-related areas.
pros: Well paid in my location. Nice office.
cons:
Huge bureaucracy and partially non-working processes. You need to have strong informal relationships to setup back-doors for delivering things in a timely fashion. Teams contain engineers with extremely different level of skills, but tasks are allocated randomly not in alignment with the skills. Not enough QAs. Thanks to this environment, a code quality could be much better. Fast delivery instead of elaborate design is everywhere.

"Agile methodologies" on a paper, chaotic development in reality. As a result, the work is looking more and more as fighting with fire.

summary: DB Risk Centre oversold and underpaid
advice: Invest in real managers both in technical and interpersonal terms. Invest in people.
pros: Berlin is a lively alternative city. Work life balance is quite good
cons:
DB Risk Centre is sold as a unique division of DB with great talents. However the level of workers is very uneven and it is not uncommon to see managers with no experience at all either managing or in banking. Turnover is incredibly high, around 1 year, which means: you go, realise it is not for you within one month and start looking somewhere else.
Many people from Italy, Spain, Greece think they are offered a good salary compared to their countries, but the truth is that it is dramatically below the average for Germany. There were legal actions against DB Risk Centre for contracting people with salaries below legal minima.
It is a compromise between Frankfurt and Mumbai: donkey work slightly cheaper than in the headquarter.

advice:
Fairly compensate those high performers through either merit raises or better bonus structure. The rigid promotion culture (1 time window, 2 year tenure minimum) is very limiting for stellar teammates to grow. 

Push for senior management investment into the IT systems to reduce system gaps and DQ issues. Finance and accounting is consistently patching reporting instead of being able to change at the source.

Keep management accountable. Promote a culture in which there is an encouraged feedback loop. The employee who voices their concern should not be a scapegoat- it discourages others to speak up.

Host company/department events to increase team morale. You can tell when folks are unhappy about their current work situation here.
pros:
Annual Leave - PTO and Vacation Allotment
Benefits (Health Insurance and 401k)
Ability to work from home 
Location - Southside
cons:
Promotion, Compensation Policy (Merit Raise, Bonus)
Data Quality and IT issues
Mismanagement - lack of concern for employees
Corporate Culture Not Defined

advice: If you could do one thing do this: close the gap between business and IT organisation
pros:
This is place where technology meets and finance. We build vast majority of technology to the bank including connectivity, pricing, risk, data warehousing. On a business there is fx, fixed income, money markets, options - so all verity of financial instruments are for you. If you enjoy finance and (server side) technology it would be the best place to work in St. Petersburg.
Company provides good opportunities for trainings including all soft of soft skills, technology skills and participating in relevant meetings.
For graduates there is amazing Java School which not only teaches with advanced (and demanded in real world) tricks in Java but also provides jobs with amazing compensations.
cons:
Getting promoted to managerial positions might be tricky in some teams (however is relatively easy in others)
Big distance to the actual business built by organisation

advice: You need more talent at the senior management levels.  Good people managers and sharp technology managers.  You need folks willing to make sweeping cultural changes and you need to stop being fearful of empowering your people.
pros: I think one of the best (and potentially worse) reasons to work with Deutsch Bank is the conservative business model that seems to have assured we didn't get whacked like so many of our peers during the economic downturn.  The other pluses are salaries, global environment and generally nice people
cons: We are about 10 years behind other tech organizations on the street.  Folks get beaten down by the fear of change into apathy.  Policies and culture are too stringent - no room for creativity or an entrepreneurial mindset.  It's not a fun place to work either as there is no sense of unified vision or camaraderie.

summary: could be an awesome place if they want it to be
advice: Compensation is fair but could be better. Bank needs to allocate more resources to the division. If the build the infrastructure of division, could be the best on the street. Some talent doesn't deserve to be there. Has a clean desk policy and forced vacation which could be a pain.
pros: this was a great place to work with a great deal of product. They have a great entrepreneurial spirit there and allow a great degree of freedom for what product you wish to sell. One of the most complete platforms to work on in the Private Client wealth business. Great product people to help with your clients. Internal competition is at a minimum. Lots of green initiatives
cons: The division is not high on the firms pecking order. No formal training. need to find things out for yourself. high degree of favoritism.

summary: Going the right direction in NC
advice: Automate the dozens of standard requests that sap time and energy from real work. Surely all the brains around here can figure out that in a compliant way?
pros:
Base salary, benefits, and 401k are top tier in the local market. Great location on Weston, solid cafe and gym on site, near greenway that connects with lots of trails. Bonus calculation was overhauled this year, last years was decent even in a rough patch for the bank. 

Software dev tooling greatly improving YoY, catching up (but not there yet) with modern practices. Moving faster than most SIFIs I would imagine.

Lots of thorny problems to solve with code, and the average caliber around you is quite high. Site represents many business lines and infrastructure functions.
cons: Paperwork during onboarding and paperwork getting a project started. Paperwork at deployment time. Paperwork getting your machine configured.

summary: Working For DB Is Like Working For A Gentle Giant. Here's why.
pros:
- Solid benefits, health insurance options are diverse with great premiums, 401(k).
- European style paid time off 
- You never know when and how frequent your body decides to punish you. Unlimited sick leave.
- Flexible work/life balance
- HR is very available and helpful.
- Constant improvements to keep up to date with the latest tech stacks
- Diversity, has a strong LGBTQ community.
- No more command & control. Mutual cooperation.
- Great exposure to various tech stacks. 
- Expert level developers in each team. I came in with 1 year of experience, experienced enough to avoid any straight out of college training, but not experienced enough to be thrown to the wolves. The wolves were actually sheep and I learned a valuable and great deal from them.
cons: - You have to "play the game" at some point and to some degree.

summary: An incredible oppoportunity that turned out to be my worst career move with my worst boss/employer in 15 years.
advice: Get to know your employees.  Not just the other senior managers.  Additionally, when employees were taking cuts in the their bonuses, it was very interesting that a senior manager was able to buy into a Cricket Team.  I'm sure he's very proud of himself.  Though clearly he has no sensitivity whatsoever to the thousands of DB employees and their families who will have to cut corners to make ends meet this year.  This might be expected from your average Trader, but not senior management and this type of ego maniac is what rules this institution.
pros: DB paid for the best talent and it has it.  They are the banks greatest asset.
cons: The bank is unable to differiniate talent, assets and egos.  It's struggling with globalization and heavy with bureacracy.  Additionally, when senior management is frequently seeking out the advice of HR it is a sign that there is something terribly wrong with a company.

advice:
- Make agile a priority bank wide
- Remove red tape for developers
- Stop treating full time developers like contractors
pros:
- you get 18 weeks of paid maternity leave if you have a child
- If you happen to get on the right team, this is not a bad place to work.
- Great medical insurance
cons:
- 1 week of paternity leave
- good teams are few and far between
- Exceptional workers are few and far between
- medical insurance is pricy
- Company is stingy with perks.  For instance, Christmas celebrations and what not came out of our own pockets, no paid first day lunch, etc.
- Developers have a lot of red tape to deal with that makes development more difficult
- Full time developers are treated as if they are another contracting agency by the business
- not enough bathrooms :)

summary: Best Place for the Ambitious Young
advice: Transparency
pros: Good benefits and compensation, opportunity to learn and advance career. Very entrepreneurial. This is really a global company with a very local feeling. The workforce is pretty young compared to other places i have observed which means the company is in tune with the coming generation. The good side about DB is that if you work hard and long, you get very paid and recognized for such efforts. Be warned, this is not a place you can hide. If you are bad at what you do, you won't advance.
cons: Long working hours, no clear leadership structure, and very independent work environment which has its pros and cons. Personally i like these downsides.

advice: Invest in technology and continue the WFH going forward. Employees will be happier in the long run
pros:
Salary, benefits, and hours are excellent for the Jacksonville area. PTO is generous.

DB is going through a transformation that is being reflected in the Jacknsoillve office. Although there have been layoffs of higher ranking individuals, DB continues to hire and promote its young talent. 

The Jacksonville office is a combination of back, middle, and front office. There is truly every type of seniority and role here.
cons:
DB is falling behind in plenty of areas. Technology is simply abysmal, they cannot remain competitive if they continue to rely on outdated infrastructure to run their business.

Work here is pretty mundane - do not expect to learn the latest technological skills in the industry.

Culture depends on the team that you are on, management likes to play favorites. More politics than the roman high court.

summary: Used to be a great place to work, but front office opportunities are dramatically worse now
advice: You need to pay better to keep great people working hard and from leaving the company. Less focus on compliance and more focus on keeping front office people happy and motivated to actually bring in revenue.
pros: Very entrepreneurial culture where one is given a lot of latitude of what can be done. Very smart coworkers. Great graduate training program.
cons: They seem to be hiring more and more compliance people by the hundreds, to the point where getting anything approved is a challenge. The red tape makes working here more and more difficult. The pay/bonuses have been dramatically reduced over the last few years to the point where it makes no sense to work here.

summary: Creates second class employees through outsourcing
advice: "Transferring" long-term employees to an outsourcing firm creates a set of employees who no longer care about the company or its future -- destroys good will.
pros: Reasonable salary/benefits and work/life balance.  Gives lip service to fostering a diverse work culture. Reasonably smart employees overall.
cons: Took advantage of market conditions and outsourced a group of long-term research employees that they needed but not longer respected to a firm with no experience in the business line, thereby creating a second-class set of de facto DB employees (as employees remained in their same desks/offices, performing the same jobs, but no longer eligible for the same benefits). Anyone who didn't accept the offer from the third rate outsourcing firm was denied severance and terminated.  Outsourcing firm has no idea how to run the business line -- completely dependent on the transferred employees to make the transaction work.

summary: Great graduate program and training, high compensation, good culture and benefits, uncertainty surrounding firm
advice: Make US investment banking strategy clear to employees, improve stability of firm and reduce negative news headlines, invest in technology to reduce lost productivity as current tech systems are subpar
pros: Great graduate training program that included global training in London which made a seamless transition from undergrad to the workforce, banking compensation is high on par with other banks, new 2 year A-to-A program, great 401k plan with employer contributions, global and diverse workforce makes for a great firm culture, lots of firm and group events
cons: Uncertainty relating to overall firm as well as US investment banking strategy, extensive negative news headlines dampen employe morale, 24/7 work culture, technology is subpar and in need of substantial investment to reduce lost productivity

advice: DB has a lot of company mantra's that promote great work/life balance.  It only applies if you are one of a very few regular staff.  The regular staff also make about $100K per year. Advantage staff start out at minimum wage or close to it. Have a threshold of about 20% permanent staff to contract staff. People will work harder knowing there is opportunity for advancement.
pros: Full-time hours and OT.  The break room has all you can drink coffee and tea free of charge but the cushions are all torn up and it's usually a mess.
cons: The bank uses mostly agency staff - Advantage Resources in Costa Mesa. Their staff is great.  However, no benefits, no vacation time, you miss a day and are put on the s list.  The VP over the vault is a dragon! Pounds on bathroom stall if you are in there too long. in the vault, only the VP and senior supervisor are permanent DB staff. The hundred other staff are at-will agency staff.

summary: Deutsche Bank - a typical investment bank
advice: Make sure junior people feel appreciated and feel like they are part of something greater.
pros: If you are lucky to have a good manager, the sky is the limit. Very enterpreneurial place. Lots of emphasis is placed on learning and training. For new associates, the first 3 months spent in training and 3 in rotations, which is really helpful as it gives one an opportunity to be introduced to various parts of the business. If you are ambtitious, driven, hard-working and willing to sacrifice your personal life for a career at least for a certain period of time, this is the place for you. Many intelligent people so one can learn a lot from them.
cons: Very hard to switch groups, so if you are unhappy, you're pretty much stuck.

advice: Look at your senior management  (VP/Directors) and use the evaluation of their direct reports to see how they are actually "managing".   The bank is cutting the workers who are actually doing the work, but not the dead weight that is apparent in the management.    Also, experienced gender discrimination when it came to promotion time.   The bank is good bank, you just have really terrible management.
pros: This place was is a good starter for your career, because you learn to do everything, since that is the only way work gets completed.  Good vacation time and benefits.
cons: The management here is the worst.  I've had good managers in the beginning, but as time went by there was a strong lack of knowledge from the management.  Careless decision making, which puts the bank at great risk.

summary: I miss working for Deutsche Bank
advice: Keep doing what you're doing.
pros:
DB was the most organized out of all of the companies I worked for. They keep up with the times, treat their employees well and there is a lot of opportunity to grow if you're the type of employee who puts 100% of yourself into your career and have something to offer.
They actually use the 5-point plan. They didn't just roll it out and work around it. It proved to be very effective. They utilized all of my skill set and challenged me to grow.
cons: DB is very competitive with talent and you really have to know how to negotiate for the salary you want. Smart on their side, but difficult if you don't know how to negotiate a good compensation package.

advice: Hire good and ethical managers.
pros: Good transport facility, every hour there is cab facility. Can expect good hike and bonus if your manager are good with you. Good brand value. Can enroll for class room trainings to enhance your skill.
cons: Most of manager you will find here working from banking domain only.  So they expect to work as they see in his previous organization, in other word they are spoiling healthy work culture of DB. They use to hire/refer their previous employers colleague irrespective of deserving or not and they will give preference to them as compare to other employees. So running project unfair way.  Highly egoistic managers. They feel like they are only owner of company as they can do what they want. You are lucky if you get a good professional manager. All the best for you guys.

advice: The change in strategy all the time doesn't leave enough time to take care about clients and their needs.
pros: I started as a graduate and worked in various strategy/ business development positions afterwards. As management changes the strategy at least every two years, there are interesting projects in strategy all the time. Most of the colleagues are great and it is fun working there. In most divisions working hours are moderate (normally not more than 10 hours a day).
cons:
As management changes it's strategy pretty often, the client is not at focus. They tried to change the corporate culture which did not (yet) work.
There are hugh differences in compensation between divisions (investment banking and the rest) and the older and younger employees. Compensation does - in many cases - not depend on performance.

summary: Good Company with Plenty of Problems Right Now (New York Office - 60 Wall Street)
advice: Reevaluate current policy regarding people and enforce internal polices to keep core people.
pros: Traditionally conservative culture. Good technical level of majority of people. All range of products and technologies you can work with.
cons: Due to huge losses in Europe, they lost a lot of people for the last 4 years and the work load for the rest is unbearable now. The pressure increased dramaticallly where the working weeks in some IT groups (in my particular) was over 70 hours/ week including weekends. People are being treated much worst than it was several years ago.  Promisses of good bonuses currently is a lie, some departments such as structured securties lost a lot of good managers and is completely mismanaged.

advice:
Few Managers are really good (fair, rational, logical, and appreciate those who deserve) - This includes my Manager. :)
Most of the managers have formed their groups. Too much of politics in terms of appraisals, increments, promotions, etc.
Please be fair and don't tolerate non-sense. It makes sense to kick out those who don't work and get a better replacement.

To be on thefair side: it's hard to keep everyone in the team happy. Let it go by being honest. Do not prefer fake promises.
pros:
1. Flexible work timings.
2. Cab facility.
3. Good exposure in terms of work.
4.  Fair ratings in terms of appraisals.
5.  Decent Salaries.
6. Good place for ladies to have work - life balanced life.
cons:
1. No Work from Home facility.
2. Lot of Politics in few teams.
3. Work allocation not uniform accross the team (few people have no work, while other have to time for lunch).

summary: Be careful about technology jobs in the US and UK
advice:
Get your act together and stop with this constant mgmt change.  Communicate clear strategy to your employees and keep to it.  

Who in their right mind is going to want to get up each day to go to work with the constant fear of layoffs to worry about.  It has been three years of this.
pros: I met some nice people at DB
cons:
Technology positions in the US and UK are being moved to India. I would think it through carefully before accepting a technology job in the US or UK.

There is constant technology senior management change. Lack of clear strategy outside of constant layoffs and cost reductions.

No salary raise for many years. What you are hired at will be your salary for years to come. Only exception is if you are promoted and you are not at the high end of the role band.

Bonuses were reduced this year by 25% from 2019 which was a poor year.

Review benefits carefully to confirm they are on par to DB peers

summary: If your in the Back Office operations and you have a silly manager, good luck to you poor fellow
advice: Please review work of your subordinates, instead of listening to their speaking skills For it is the productivity that matters to you more than verbal skills. If your subordinates are not up to the mark, work with them to understand for yourself (without prejudice and influence) where the problem arises and how to have it solved.
pros: You get a very good exposure to various financial products/services. Have great client interactivity and within the organisation.
cons: Workload is too much, and if you are under a manager who does not recognise your capabilities rather recognises you for chatting him up, then you may not have a great career life in this organisation.

summary: Very good, but could be better
pros:
Great corporate culture - you feel proud to be a part of company.
Office and working place of highest standard.
Great benefits package.
Competitive compensation level (at least by the time of hiring - see details in Cons)
International team and a lot of cutting-edge challenging problems to solve.
cons:
A lot depends on your direct management. And it's a matter of good chance to get one that will help you to implement your career potential.
Questionable employee retention policy - a company rather hire new employee than raise compensation for existing employee to the same level thus doing little to retain experienced worker.
Periodic serious organizational changes leave some good initiatives half-done.
Inertia due to various level of internal bureaucracy is high, which is quite natural for the companies of such size and level.

summary: Enormous amount of work, limited advancement
advice: Personal empire building yet continues even with a new Co-CEO and management structure.  For the future restrict personal empire building.
pros: Lot of work, large scale projects in the pipeline. Potential to learn a lot. LArge focus on people esp. within the smaller locations.  Power center is in London, NY and Frankfurt, so try to be in one of these locations (esp. at the VP and above leve;l). Lot of lateral movement of people.
cons:
Complete focus on costs.  No promotions above VP possible without significant fat-letting. Fragmented organization with personal fiefdoms.  Internal costs have skyrocketed esp. in tech where the duplication of functions across IT groups means that your job is done twice and then checked.  
Recent oeprational excellence had created confusion in the ranks.
