summary: Good starting point for getting into the industry
advice: More needs to be done to retain valuable workers. Many good employees leave due to the inability to move up or get promotions/raises.
pros:
Good starting place when entering BSA/AML Field and getting time in the industry
Knowledgeable co-workers
Good work is noticed and appreciated
Lateral movement is relatively easy
cons:
Promotions are a once a year deal, so if you didn't make the list, you have to wait a full year, which also means you won't be considered for higher positions within the company for another year. 
Raises are basically non-existent. You hear from most prior employees that they left in order to get a pay bump.
Very little retention, you end up with many different managers in a year, which can be difficult to establish yourself as a valuable worker.

summary: Overall a good place to work, good experience.
advice: Don't make rash decisions with out knowing exactly what the group / people in it are involved with.  Much talent was lost and quality of certain services reduced.  (Possible that I don’t see the full picture, and that those services are no considered valuable).  But it’s not uncommon to see teams try to fill the knowledge gap and shoulder the responsibilities of the dismissed group or individual.
pros: Strong, solid company.  Many opportunities within.
cons: It really matters which group you work for.  Some groups are very disconnected from the positive culture DB tries to instill.  I went through many different departments; my review would be much more negative, if I would not find a different opportunity (within the company).

advice: Do something about the culture of no differentiation for performance, but retain the freedom and flexibilty that comes from the fact that our people are all very different rather than the clones of other Financial Services firms - like Goldman, for example. Find a way to make the most of the people you manage to attract.
pros:
Great people
Space to shape your own role
Flexibility to do things our own way
Diversity of individuals, not a "clone copy" of one another
Very global thinking and acting
International opportunites
Career mobility if you manage it yourself
Survived the market crash well
Pretty good pay compared to some competitors
cons:
Disorganised
Slow decision making
Not a meritocracy - promotions and pay are political
Pay not linked to performance
Poor senior leadership
Our of date technology and processes
Short term initiatives rather than long term strategies

advice: The low morale seems to be a systemic issue, rather than one deriving solely from the current financial situation. There is also a substantial lack of transparency within the compliance department.
pros: Great benefits as an American employee; probably the best at a bulge bracket firm. Additionally, at least in the Jacksonville office, a very reasonable work-life balance. If an attorney, the bank will cover bar dues and continuing education costs.
cons: Entering into the bank at a time of severe financial difficultly has imposed restraints in both upward and lateral mobility. Compensation is at the lower end of the industry standard, and the Bank is reluctant to provide compliance officers with continuing education (Series licenses; CFA; etc). Working in the nearshore office comes across as a decision negatively impacting career growth opportunities.

advice: The goals set are great, but the tools to achieve those goals could improve (systems training, product knowledge, introduction to other areas connected to business line would be useful). If someone wants to add value and want to improve processes, provide a pathway, system, or process to allow them to help DB become better. Especially, if someone is willing to do it on their own time.
pros: Much support from management. Resources for learning and personal growth everywhere. Diversity and Inclusion is important to this company. Working on solutions is primary. Having the difficult conversations to build a positive future are central. Best family leave to have a child that I've seen in a while.
cons: Long hours and not enough headcount in some areas.

advice: Resign, you have all proven since the start of Covid that you dont have the basic skills to even organise sending out a thank you letter to overworked staff at christmas.  No empathy or understanding for staff through a pandemic. Staff working in their bedrooms during covid getting mails from higher management complaining how tough it was to set up an office in their huge houses in Howth and Donegal.
pros: VHI paid for staff. No other pros.
cons: No financial support for WFH. Expected to use all own equipment and maintain same productivity levels. Toxic management with bullying rampant. Micro management where every last second is accounted for. Recent redundancy process deeply flawed. Management gave contradicting information to staff on dates and packages. Dublin staff who were told being made redundant were cc'd on emails about the bank making $1billion plus in profit. A horrible company focused on the bottom line and couldn't care less about their staff.

summary: Unhealthy, intimidating behavior by senior management, Work life balance is pathetic
advice:
Respect your employees & talent.
Don't blame your resources for the fault that you have committed. 
Work life balance is important . Dont only showcase in your organizational emails.
pros: They might offer you good salary but that could be a trap in your career.
cons:
A boss is someone who leads and drives their teams and groups and not an authoritative figure who shouts and imposes to scare people to work.
If your boss has any connection with you then you will get recognized if you don't work as well.
No work life balance.
Pathetic managers who don't know how to run projects
Insultating words will make you mentally weak. 
Work culture is toxic in nature. Old employees play dirty politics and never share any knowledge as they afraid of losing their value. New employees are harassed by old employees.
Higher Management is incompetent
 Unhealthy, intimidating behavior by senior management when it comes to personal interactions
Not Recommended for senior folks.

advice: Break down silo's. The strategy of silo's works in the rapid growth stage- but needs to be fixed in the consolidation pahse, specially when market conditions are challenging
pros: Very dynamic organization- rapid pace of change and development. Very good at innovation. Led by a bunch of smart people specially on the glabal markets side. Good strategy to sustain in the long run.
cons: Highly silo'ed environment- minimal cooperation when working on cross-divisional initiatives. Poor infrastructural and control platforms- chances of a Soc-gen like scenario are not remote. Not a very structured promotion process- possible to get windfall gains from one good year's performance without the ability to sustain that performance in the long run. Low on work-life balance. Center of power largely in Frankfurt, low influence/image iN US.

summary: Horrible Management in Lower Levels that comes from Upper Management in New York
advice: Please survey employees reporting to the AVPs within CLM for a more accurate reflection of these managers and their unfairness when it come to direct reports that are not liked  for whatever reasons.  These managers are constantly talked about by their direct reports with no one having the courage to come forward with complaints.  it’s not a good environment for some employees
pros: Good benefits,  nice office space
cons: You have to suck up to unprofessional local management in Jacksonville in order to “fit in” and be acknowledged.  Managers in Jacksonville seem to have two faces with one being used for upper management and a nasty one being used for direct reports.

summary: Deutsche Bank is a pretty good place to work
advice: Help foster cross-group communications so that we feel more like one company solving problems together.
pros: Stable, high salaries, fast-paced. It is a large company so lots of opportunity to move around.  Good perks such as 401k matching, pension, vacation days, free museum access, etc. There's a surprising amount of independance of how to solve problems here.
cons: It can be beurocratic and slow-to-act. Management ability varies widly.  Deutsche Bank's corporate culture, at least in the New York region, was to be cowboys - we were encouraged to do whatever possible to get the job done as soon as possible. Later, after the Bankers' Trust/Alex Brown acquisition there was too much process. Only now are we starting to get a good balance.

summary: You will find yourself working late hours in a very employee unfriendly environment so I cannot recommend DB.
advice: Please take some time to listen to your employees and compensate them fairly for their hard work and dedication.
pros:
- Some positions give you the opportunity to travel.  Deutsche Bank has office locations in many countries across the globe.
- Typical large company benefits. Medical, Dental, Vision
- 3-4 weeks paid vacation, depending on position.
cons:
-  You are expected to work very late hours.  Not very work - life balance friendly.
-  Salary adjustments and promotions given once a year across the entire bank. No exceptions.
-  Very strict compliance department. You must move all bank, 401k, IRA, etc accounts into Deutsche Bank accounts.
-  Upper management spends needlessly and is not efficient at controlling costs
-  Not employee friendly and management is terribly inefficient.
-  Staff is not rewarded or given credit for hard work / Your performance is not linked to your salary

summary: Excellent place to work - until you get let go due to downsizing.
pros: Good benefits, people, use of technology  and nice work areas.  Very professional culture.  People I have worked with and worked for have been hard working, take their responsibilities seriously and expect others to act the same way.  Hard work is rewarded.
cons: No job security.  Title/years of service don't matter.  If they need to save money by reducing headcount, everybody's head is on the chopping block.  But I'm sure that is true everywhere.  Workload can be heavy.  I worked a lot of overtime just to keep up as an admin, analysts seemed to live there.

summary: Nice place to work for Entry-level careers
advice: Recognize the workers for their performance and don't emphasize mistakes more than accomplishments. Also, higher wages would be nice.
pros:
The benefits are outstanding, medical, dental, vision, and vacation days. Interacting and meeting new people from around the world is very interesting and a great learning experience. 
This is a good career for an entry level position, in the finance industry and also if you want to gain experience.
cons:
The pay is not good, for the workload and the expectations that is put on our plates. Loads of pressure to be perfect not humans.
Outsourcing is a huge issue. Saving money does not always ensure quality for the clients. Duh!
Extremely high turnover, which should cause a light bulb to go off to upper management.

advice:
Improve the hiring process and hire the right people for the right positions.
Create a mechanism to allow feedback from direct reports on people managers' performance.
pros:
Nice office, although I personally have never found the time to use the play rooms.
Various training programs, although these are available only after 6 months of employment.
Work for home option - 4 days a month.
Free & good coffee and tea.
cons:
Low technical knowledge level in most of the teams.
Organizational chaos - roles and responsibilities are not always clear. Often ended up doing lower level tasks than what was described in the role description.
A lot of waste in the so-called “agile” projects.
No mechanism to share feedback on your direct line manager’s performance.
Long working hours, including weekend, in some projects.

advice: Middle management need to develop their own technical knowledge of the functions they take on from overseas in order to manage effectively.
pros: Good health insurance and one of the best pension benefits 15% of your salary once you're over 30 or reach Associate level. Growing presence in Ireland
cons: Lack of technical skills, management keen to take on work from overseas offices without the prerequisite technical knowledge of the work necessary to maintain levels of service for clients (service centre mentality focused on keeping costs low, growth based on outsourcing from abroad). The office needs to develop clear employee development and progression paths in order to retain talent. Salaries at the lower end of the industry

advice: perhaps triaining for managers so that they actually can properly guide the careers of motivated employees as opposed to selecting only "high potential" candidates towards increased responsibilities and growth.
pros: Flexibility in your work situation and remote access is great.  Many colleagues work from home at least one day per week-this is great for working parents.  There are many great programs relating to cultural diversity that promote and enhance a very inclusive environment for staff.
cons: DB has the potential to be an exceptional environment for real growth and development, however there is way to go before that becomes a reality.  Current management changes, ongoing upheaval and outsourcing makes this difficult. This puts undue stress on staff who are looking for guidance and direction.

advice: Do think about how you are going to achieve what you are trying to achieve.  The new people culture that you are bringing in isn't going to take you there.
pros: The money is/was good.  The bank is now trying hard to be a technology company, but not sure how successful it would be.
cons:
The bank had never been a technology company, and had heavily relied on its outsource partners.  However, in the recent months it is trying hard to be a technology company and trying to bring in expertise and intellectual property.  But in doing so, the culture within the bank has taken a back seat.  It is not the same place anymore.
Work life balance is taking a back seat.

summary: A way too much politics in NYC office.
advice:
To get a new multicultural and multinational leaders to follow in NYC. Stop current hiring model -  "let me bring a friend of a friend who I like, even I know the friend is not qualified for a job at all".
To focus on people, to build an open team environment and cooperation within all team members as well as other teams
pros: to gain global experience in your area of work and work with multiple teams globally
cons:
-Bad management overall in NYC (not qualified for work at all) and nothing is being done by the senior management
-HR does not support employees. Most of HR reps are external to the bank and don't want to get involve in anything
-Old, difficult systems and processes to navigate
-A way too much politics in NY office. It is expected to have politics everywhere, but DB NY politics can be champions in it if nothing else

advice: More work from home flexibility would be nice.
pros: Awesome benefits! Great pay! The Cary location is really investing in creating a community. There are employee engagement groups that work hard to make this a great place to work! I am working in cutting edge technologies and the company seems to want to invest in their employees and in employee retention. The office space is very nice including an onsite cafe and gym.
cons: There is less flexibility than in most tech companies I have worked for. At the Cary location, you can work from home on occasion, when necessary, but most people are in the office most days. It is a bank. As should be expected, there are security and process requirements that can impede your job efficiency.

advice: make sure sales associates are being treated well by their brokers.... and if not, do not threaten their employment, try to pair them up with someone who they are more compatible with.
pros:
Deutsche Bank itself is a top three investment bank and is a great resume builder
Benefits are great
Managing Directors and Management are accessible for questions and information 
Depending on business of broker you work with, job can be extremely diverse, high pressured, and a great challenge
cons:
Being  a Sales Associate is a dead end position, so make sure you love what you do and who you work with
Promotion within the firm from this role is difficult and not necessarily encouraged 
Brokers do not always respect the associate role and the amount of work actually involved.

summary: Not a technology organization in India at the least and there is no scope for career growth or advancement of skills;
advice: You will have to hire, respect , promote and grow technologist in your organization , or all you get is poor cadre of management which is solely reliant on vendors for technology consulting , resulting in huge costs for new sw, poor quality systems and very high life cycle costs , as is the case now
pros: Global Organization, Great Market forray, Technology focused for Systems and Processes
cons: Highly Bureaucratic, most management is technology illiterate, technologist are just preferred for adhoc tech help not for working on strategic long term goals of systems , life cycles and their data and load thresholds

advice: The pay is the most blatant issue for the Jax office. There's also the fact that communication and travel between Jax and NY can often be shoddy and advancement opportunities seem fairly limited.
pros: Very intelligent and cooperative coworkers, more laid back atmosphere than the location on Wall St. Management is in general good at directing day to day activities.
cons: The Jax office is turning into an analyst churn shop. They are underpaying 2-3yr analysts and first year associates big time. In fact, brand new interns are making more on an adjusted basis than 3rd year analysts due to the company moving interns to the new higher pay scale while leaving existing employees on the older, lower scale.

summary: good to be in, hard to grow out
advice:
(1) Planning horizon is factually limited to 1 year due to financials and people "retention" + (2) inefficient change management + (3) lots of legacy systems = all changes are just tactical or are strategic ideas reduced down to a few tactical 1y steps that are legacy when finished. 

Without #1 or #2 (or both) solved, #3 will continue to grow making the situation harder with every year.
pros: good people, lots of opportunities to take on (if you dare), open-door style of Moscow dev center management, medical insurance and other perks. And many growth opportunities, but growth is slow.
cons: very-very-very slow changes, terrible change management of Bank in overall, illusionary long-term planning, domain architects changed every 1-2 years.

summary: Upper Management is inconsistent (or lacking in vision); reliance on the young and abusing H1-B
advice: Decide on a vision; communicate it to employees and customers; and finally, stick with it for longer than 6-12 months--preferably 3-5 years.
pros:
Great benefits
Fairly fast advancement for entry/low-level employees
Strong support for diversity (nationality, gender, LGBT...)
cons:
Inconsistent upper-management decisions/vision (layoffs quickly followed by panic hiring)
Lack of advancement for those at the Assistant Vice President level
Overuse/Abuse H1-B visas system
Have to leave company to advance salary/title for more than low level employees
Under-appreciation in the tech divisions for Financial Analysts
Extremely tight cost controls, including late year changes to vacation benefits 
Cramped and noisy working enviroment
Tech workers given "virtual desktops"-machines
Upper management extremely late to handle prior ethical lapses
HR represents the company, and does little for the employee

summary: Great place with a few flaws
advice: Seriously...take a look at the middle management.  We are moving away from focusing on the job and getting more into nasty politics.  Vision in the right direction, but the middle management has too many incompetent managers.  Other than that...thanks for making DB's technology group such a great place to work.
pros:
--Great Pay
--Good vision by senior management
--Global presence
--Incredible place to start your career through their graduate program
--People with diverse backgrounds
--Business understands the value of technology
--Mobility encouraged and promoted
--Spends money for social causes
--Great benefits
--More vacation time than you can spend
cons:
--Senior management comes up with brilliant ideas, but picks morons to implement them
--Middle management (VP/Director) level is full of nasty politics
--Complete lack of diversity in upper management (mostly male and white)

advice: I must say I was very satisfied with how the managers worked personnel-wise. DB should deleverage fast though.
pros: The Deutsche Bank is a company with a truly global presence and as such it is very international even in Frankfurt am Main. Also, it offers good opportunities to advance on your career within the company. Also, having DB on your Curriculum Vitae after an internship makes at least the German employers drool.
cons: The working hours are sometimes pretty long, plus it has a somewhat bad reputation as a company in Germany, so you sometimes get into discussions about people who are motivated to express their opinion about DB. I also think that their recruiters really stand out with their somewhat bloated jargon.

summary: Overall a good place to work
advice: Don't let cost cutting pressure mean that you lose good people.  Make more effort to keep people appraised of why decisions are being made and how it will affect them.
pros: Great pay, stable company, has performed relatively well in the global crisis. High caliber people.  Deutsche Bank treats its people well and is committed to providing work-life balance, where possible.
cons: Stodgy German culture, difficult to make changes, global nature of the firm sometimes difficult to negotiate. Management are under enormous pressure to cut costs, and mange one quarter at a time, making long term investment in infrastructure difficult.  Good people are let go to cut costs and then have to be replaced at a later date.

advice: Change the politics in the office. Peoples careers being played with to get one over on other managers. They work they people who work hard and expect more and more. While those who do nothing or are incapable get away with little work. Pay is awful. Bonus is non existent. No pay rise in three years. And very much turning into a sexist environment.
pros: Nice people. Flexible. Ok facilities.
cons: Poor management from top down. Promotion process is terrible. Pay and bonus way below par. Director recently compared pay to AIB BOI and other RETAIL banks. Miles off the mark. Expect way too much from you. Can never get their deadlines right. Always a panic. So many policy changes. Too many chiefs.

summary: Stuffy work environment but with global possibilities
advice:
- Hire younger energetic people with good ideas
- Give people enough for them to be vested in actual improvements but not long enough for them to be regarded as indispensable or rulers of their kingdoms
- Document processes more effectively and be more transparent on performance metrics with all reports. Especially in cases where performance cannot be simply measured but must be gauged by VOC, etc
pros:
- Stable work environment
- Global outreach for personal development and career options
- Interesting people to work with
cons:
- Stifling work environment sometimes : pseudo innovation rewarded rather than actual improvements
- Lethargic on technology changes
- In India, DB has a very nepotistic and "arse-licky" culture, especially in the back offices

summary: Sales Support  - Asset Management, limited opportunity for growth, ineffective departmental management
advice: My manager was afraid of his manager, there was little opportunity to change ineffective policies or suggest changes. I think subordinates should be allowed to blindly review their manager and peers.
pros: Good work/life balance, rarely worked late or from home, opportunities to interact with senior investment professionals
cons: Fear-based culture, peers are afraid to point out errors or recommend process improvements, hard work is not rewarded, environment is too casual for those with a drive to succeed, co-workers strove to do as little work as possible and take short-cuts which was what our manager wanted as well. Lack of communication and apathy led to many errors. Not rewarding career-wise.

advice:
Walk the talk, or rather sprint ahead of everybody else, particularly with respect to saving programs - if you expect everybody down the line to cut back, get rid of your own privileges first, including the culture of "exemptions" and "exceptions".

If you want to be taken seriously with respect to gender diversity (also by the women who work for you), consider to get at least one alibi woman onto the actual or into the extended board cycle. Ensure there are women in all divisional executive and in other global committees.

When you separate from employees, or employees separate from you, improve exiting procedures: Leavers are potential future employees and usually they are also clients and stakeholders. Unless someone is fired because of misconduct, a thank you letter by management can make a big difference. A job certificiation that is not signed off by two admin dudes from outsourced HR Online and contains a wrong spelling of name and incorrect job title will show a certain degree appreciation. Not kicking people out like dogs when they are laid off can as well - if you had reason to trust them to this day, you can risk to trust them a few hours longer. Also, employees are free to resign when they think it is time to do so. They do not do it to hurt their boss or to sabotage the team (at least, usually they don't), so there is no reason to let bad feelings overshadow the last weeks.
pros:
Working with some of the highliest skilled people in the industry with expansion in some of the most interesting markets.

Very diverse staff, client, product and operating platform

Comparatively good staff benefits

Ongoing growth and opportunities particularly in Asia (despite of onsite job cut-downs due to ongoing smart- and outsourcing of processes into low-payment hubs in Manila, Berlin, Mumbai, New Jersey etc)
cons:
Global senior management in Deutsche continues to very much be an old boy's club, chauvinism is omnipresent at this level, and gender discrimination is very common in mid and senior levels and part of the company culture (despite official policies and speeches). Similar discrepancies between official and inofficial company cultural values in many other areas.

As an MD or Dir, be prepared to deal with a comparatively high rate of politics and silo-mentality standing in the way of efficiency and bank-wide cooperation

Experimental minor and major restructurings, which often are short-sighted unaligned measures of pure activism, are ever present. Many things tend to go back to where they were after a certain amount of time - of course, as in many places, going back to former solutions is usually sold as yet another big innovation, not as a strategic mistake being corrected. Low buy-ins into and unspoken boycots of restructuring measures by mid and senior managers as a result.

Recent year cost cutting programs and smartsourcing of jobs result in overall low job morale, resignation and frustration.

summary: High Tech Labor Salvery.. too much bureaucracy.. too much panic all the time (Assistant VP)
advice: Have some "American Spirit" , this is America not London or India!
pros:
It's situated in calm and peaceful Cary, NC
Bonus ( If you are are good in internal bureaucracy and manage to get it!)
cons:
In over 15 years of my IT career I have never seen such bad work atmosphere with so much panic and work pressure from chain of managers over you. Everybody is president , vice presidents and managers.. too less people who really work.. so of course work pressure... That's what managers are for right? Make tech slave labor work. or how else managers will get big bonuses?

Their new policy is to lure tech guys from other countries or other states to leave their good jobs dreaming big bonuses and peaceful life , come to this remote location of Cary...then make them work like slaves. Hire one senior tech guy and then hire four beginners so that this experienced guy will actually teach the beginners everything and even DO their job... as they are "no-vice".. so make sure you are not that "experienced guy"

This is not a bank. It's a bank's IT development center. So basically we develop applications for bank. So it works like a IT shop with all the crap that comes with it....

Every body ready to cut your throat to get anybody out of his bonus way. Everybody looks like in pressure and panic state.
If you are looking for great work atmosphere and peaceful life where you can work and do some innovative work then DON'T come to this Cary Development Center.
Only join this center , if you just want good pay and bonuses...but you should be ready to take this much stress, panic , and ready to be micro managed by omnipresent managers.

summary: Good place to start a career
advice: None
pros: Co-workers are generally friendly & intelligent and there are plenty of after work events.  Managers make themselves accessible.  New analyst training program in London is top notch and most expenses are paid.  Compensation compares well with most other banks (new ops analysts get overtime).  Good name recognition in the industry.  DB has been less affected by the financial crisis than many competitors.
cons: Jobs are being outsourced to lower cost locations (India).  Some people have tremendous egos.  Hours can be long.  There is limited mobility between the back and front office.  Wall Street office is nice, but the area gets lonely late at night.

advice: As a recommendation to senior management, more emphasis should be placed on the build-up of new talents within the organization as well as more transparency around business lines' strategies.
pros: Deutsche Bank provides excellent opportunities for professional growth based upon the opportunities presented from very early on.  Employees have the opportunity to prove themselves from very early on and take on a wide remit of work.
cons: In terms of career advancement and financial rewards for the level of work performed, this has not been entirely satisfactory.  It seems, as in most companies, the number of years of experience is given precedence over the level / complexity of work managed and projects successfully delivered.

summary: Safe haven to hide and die as a specialist
advice: Perform a thorough employee clean-up based on merit and value they deliver. Be more result-oriented rather than process-oriented.
pros:
Good compensation in comparison with other software companies
Possibility to have very little control over yourself if you play right.
Good people.
cons: Non result-oriented and highly political environment. People spend enormous amount of time on meaningless discussions. It is absolutely possible and widely encouraged to get promotions and salary increases just by feeding bulls..t to senior management. Many good specialists, who could otherwise deliver some value, figure this out and become highly paid politicians. Not to mention a wide layer of mediocre staff who just hide there doing nothing.

advice: Operating in different timezones across the global is quite a challenge - having the opportunity to meet our counterparts across the globe whether by video conference or face-to-face; once a quarter would be an amazing opportunity.
pros:
DB is a culturally diverse company.  In my opinion - management believes in the culture and values and it is expected that we all have a 'Passion to Perform'.
The company has no glass ceilings and growth to many different career paths.
The benefits package is awesome.
cons: My only complaint is about the organizational chart.  DB is a global organization but management is not always local - seeing the people you work with and work for would be really helpful.

advice: If you start assessing managers by attrition rates of their teams, you'll very quickly be able to assess real performance.  Weed out managers who can't build and keep teams.  Focus on rewarding strong performers. Many of us wanted to stay at DB for the broader opportunities within the company, but could no longer tolerate our manager's abuse or incompetence.
pros: Deutsche Bank is a great name brand to have on your CV.
cons: The Ireland/ East Point branch of DB is poorly managed. In one year, a team of 20 people that started together, 18 have left. All of this due to low morale and incompetent managers that devalue employees.

advice: While group management is making an effort to improve the infrastructure of the firm,  make an even bigger effort to improve the culture.   Get into the weeds and increase dialogs with the "worker bees" that make the bank run.   Bring in more talent from other firms that can bring a fresh perspective to processes that may improve the overall control function and culture of the firm.
pros: If there are pros for the firm,  it's few and far between.   The best thing about the New York office is a small pocket of employees who are new to the firm that actually try to make a difference.   While they are a small force,  the frustration increases day by day.   It is a common to say "we're up a creek without a paddle".
cons: Two words can pretty much summarize the firm -  accountability and fragmentation.  The culture,  at least in the NYC office,  is one of political finger pointing which lead to a lack of accountability by mid-level and senior managers.   This lack of accountability even for simple concepts such as  "best practices" is affected by this culture.   This also leads to fragmentation - everyone out for themselves instead of helping to improve the culture and the current state of the firm.

summary: Good for starting your career or you don't have an university title
advice: Stop hiring or promoting people without a living cert to be the boss of an MBA owner!
pros: Good private pension contributions if you are 30 yrs old or above. Good salary, considered the low complexity of work. Very friendly environment with your pairs. HR team will help you if you want to move to another team or branch.
cons: Your tasks will be very repetitive. Low training is provided because you boss most of the time doesn't know himself the bank's products and the HR don't want to pay for external training. Expect a lot of bureaucracy, which mainly doesn't come from Germany but from your line manager, who will be obsessed about control. He/she will create tasks that are not related to your work just to check on you. The Dublin site is considered bad by other branches all around the world. Hence, colleagues from other branches can treat you very badly. The offices are based in the Eastpoint business park which is impossible to reach. The food from the canteen is low quality and the selection is poor.

advice: If you really want to have a reputation as being family friendly, this attitude / approach should be distributed from the top down.
pros: It seems pretty difficult to differentiate most of the larger investment banks from each other, but I believe Deutsche Bank is well respected on the Street.  Salaries are competitive.
cons: Similar to all banks, but also depending on what group you work in, a 40-hour work week is unrealistic.  You get paid well, but you're expected to work long hours to finish the job.  You get 5 weeks of vacation time / personal days, but I don't know anyone who would actually be bold enough to use all the allotted vacation time--face time is much more important.  Similarly, even though the company offers flex time and working from home arrangements, I'm not sure I would be willing to pursue those options for fear of jeopardizing the quality of my bonus.  Lastly, the cubicles are uncomfortably tiny (they are so short they only come up to your neck), so there's not much privacy.

advice: Wake up and pay attention to your employees. You neglect the day-to-day and pile on testing that only serves to make you look good to your superiors. You lie to your employees to cut costs and look good for your managers.
pros:
Pay was better than any other place in the area.

Benefits were really great.
cons:
Senior management is playing the politics game and you are not a part of it. They tell you one thing to your face and turn around and mumble the opposite into their headsets.

Your reviews are also politics-driven and don't have anything to do with your actual performance. Get a bad review, you can't advance for another 2 years.

Work/life balance means zilch if you aren't management. Your managers will happily work from home 3 days a week and take whatever days off they please, but you are out of luck and get talked out of taking off.

DB's"Values" are just its way of making itself feel good, they mean nothing in daily practice.

My specific team's managers lied to us about holiday compensation, in order to cut costs and deceive us into taking less money on holidays we were required to work. 

DB is a sinking ship, don't bother.

summary: Great on a resume, but major restructuring due to cost cutting measures
advice: Hire more staff to help deal with the volumes that you know are coming with the Clearing Business resulting from Dodd-Frank. Respect that not everyone on staff is comfortable with working 11 hours every day and may actually have obligations outside of work.
pros: Great resume experience, ability to run projects, multi-functional cross team work, great benefits packages
cons: Very little respect or sympathy for work-life balance. Average work day is 9-11 hours, depending on volume, market circumstances, and time of the year. They will pay you less than industry standard if you're not an AVP or higher. Once you advance to a Senior Analyst role, there is little room for movement as there are not often positions opened above you. Can be difficult to move laterally to another department for a new opportunity - more than once during my time there, the departments underwent a hiring freeze for several months or more and that meant you couldn't move anywhere. VERY fast paced environment - this is not a job where you will have time to deal with many personal matters during the day.

advice:
It became circus when I was there. Estalished a team then they expected huge amount of cross training then they wanted staff saves then location move. All at once with no time to breath.
Technological updates are required. People should be focusing on process improvement rather than technology problems.
Need to make HR and IT dept efficient to help ur people work.
pros: Challenging environment to work. So you build up nerve for unorganised environment.
cons:
1. Systems are not in good shape. There are a lot of systems to learn before u learn process. 
2. Application are out of date. DB is still using SSR.
3. Extra pressure on people managers as there are no team leaders. Managers r expected to do TL plus Manager job.
4. Lot of politics.
5. Performance evaluation is not transparent.
6. Human resources department is not efficient at all.
7. IT dept doesn't know what to do with most of the applications plus they work at a snail's speed to resolve any iT issues.
8. Getting application for my staff was big headache. It used to take 2 to 3 months for an employee to get full access to required applications. Massive pain area.

advice: Hire sensible guy as manager. Don't look that they are US returns guy. VP position are going to those who don't deserve that.
pros: Policy Is Good, Free Cab Facility
cons:
I am having 10 years of experience and I can say truly that I have seen worst management in Deutsche Bank. People who are at VP position thinks that they are the intelligent people on this earth and never come into the picture if team is facing any issue. They always say We as a team but if there will be anything related to work they will say You.

Some VP here are Technical Architect and they will proudly say that they are Technical Architect but they don't know the penny of anything regarding the project. And will put developer only into KT session, Requirement gathering, Designing part. And will never be seen through out the project lifecycle. Only Developers are responsible for entire project. Not only that they Think developer needs to be multi productivity and multi-role guy. He has to work not only in one project but he has to handle multiple project and also need to work as tester and someday has to work as SL2 guy.

For the first time I have given the review on glass door coz of this situation in my entire career and you can think how worst management is here.

advice: Just shoot this dying horse - it would be a mercy killing.
pros: Thank goodness for my coworkers.  I would've gone crazy a long time ago.  An atmosphere like this allows the malcontents to find each other.
cons: This company is so big that EAs are just used to manage calendars, book meetings and submit expense reports.  Before the ban on travel (due to cost cutting measures) I used to get to do that too but no mas as of the past year.  Information is disseminated via gossip, not discussions with managers.  So many long term employees are just milking the teat - "working" from home, hiring consultants to do their job, not being held accountable for little, yet important things, like not responding to emails.  The IT Helpdesk is a disaster because no one actually wants to follow through with anything.  All of the in-house systems are counter intuitive so much so that I think they were designed to eff with people.  The offices are run down and borderline gross - there is always a light bulb out somewhere - and the people in the Jersey City office do not dress professionally (to say the least).  Any office non-EU is treated like a red-headed stepchild and there is an air of superiority wafted over from The Fatherland.

advice: Fish begins to stink at the head. Critically reconsider RTC management performance and value every manager personnaly added  to the organization. It is time for big change.
pros: Excellent office space, competitive payrate, good medical insurance
cons:
RTC management team is exclusive club for those who think only about themselves and how to preserve the position and power. Zero chances to be promoted to D-level if you are not member of this club. Double standards, unfair treatment of your contribution. Since RTC management team has only stars in it, bonus pool (which decreases every year) majorily distributed amongst this team.

Russia Technology Center is typical realization of team extension model and every manager coming from UK, US or Germany communicate on the every townhall "do you freaking JIRAs". So the only function RTC management team does is harassing everyone to get JIRAs done by all means on time to satisfy higher-ups abroad. If project is accidentally owned and executed in RTC it usually becomes chaotic and fire-fighting activity. No surprise as Russia Technology Center management destroyed Project Management Community of Practice and let all project managers go to the competitor Bank.

summary: Swing and miss approach to banking
advice: Stop the hand-wringing and the platitudes and commit to actual, effective change.  No one wants yet another buzz-word or initiative that will be abandoned or scaled back quietly in six months time.  Everyone wants a title and responsibility but no one wants to be accountable.  Risk has brought in senior MDs from other European banks who have not made a single bit of difference other to increase the cost base and the red tape.  US employees are treated like the help while the pompous Brits and pedantic Germans continue to do things the same old way with the same old results.  Take a lesson from your US peers.
pros:
Flexible work arrangements
Solid mobile options (dbiOS)
Ability to own huge books of work (because no one else wants them)
cons:
Firm claimed no bonuses would be paid (then paid billions in "retention packages" to certain employees) - we all get to suffer for the sins of a few
Garbage performance compared to peers 
Massively hampered by EU / German-specific regs while American peers eat our lunch

advice: Lack of good management can create a sense of "doesn't anybody know what they're doing around here?".  I understand you are a bank and control is important, but the bureaucracy is stifling and very counterproductive.
pros: They usually try to do the right thing (the trading scandals aside).  The company is progressive.  If you end up in a good niche in the company, you can learn a lot and benefit in your career.
cons: It is a troubled institution right now and not a very fun place to work.  There are not a lot of good managers, just individuals who worked their way up the ladder through outlasting other employees.

advice: Your people can only perform well if they have the necessary training, time in position and clear expectations. It's not all about social networking. Some people just want to do their job and get ahead by hard work instead of playing politics all the time.
pros: Huge amount of diversity and great acceptance of others. They have great benefits and the salary is at least on par if not better in most cases. Free coffee.
cons: It's an investment bank and it's all about the money. Can be very stressful. Training is usually lacking or non existent. Expectations can be unreasonable by management but there is always someone willing to point the finger in times of trouble.

jobTitle: Vice President Heaf of Human Resources Solutions
advice:
They have set and communicated clear strategies until 2020. It is important for them to stay focused in the achievement of the goals they have set, 
maintain open lines with its employees to retain talents, and simplify way of doing business.
pros: Working in DB is great because I got to work with really smart and brilliant professionals. Its current CEO John Cryan maintains regular communication with employeess with high degree of sincerity. There is a strong sense of empowerment and employees are given the opportunity to pursue creative solutions to problems and seek career progression.  DB also invests significantly in employee's professional and personal development.
cons: DB still needs to work on improving systems integration to achieve its desired operational efficiencies.

advice:
restore some form of merit based promotion and remuneration policy and actually implement it.
Actually provide some leadership and direction to the local franchise.  Give people a reason to be proud to work for DB again.
pros:
competitive remuneration, especially for new joiners
It once was a very strong and proud player in the Australian market
cons:
The bank globally is in very tough times, share price has tanked.
Below VP level there is very little bonus inventive - capped at 3-4% across the board and not reflective of individual performance
Promotion is next to impossible - usually a 2-3 year process and very unlikely in Australia
Australian franchise is downsizing resulting in poor culture and low morale
Year on year reduction on total compensation - expected to do more with less.
There is often a large salary disparity between people doing the same role.
Poor senior leadership - usually too interested in managing their own career rather than looking after their employees

advice: Improve your communication at all levels, be more aware of the change and come with quick reponses to situations, Be innovative
pros: Diverse, detailed processes, great brand name, understanding the current organisational context, doing well in recessionary times, continously challenging the status quo, gives challenging assignments, opportunities in your home country as well as abroad, very subject matter expertise oriented
cons: Risk averse and bureucratic in certain situations, as it is very sme oriented it is a very silo fdriven organisation with matrix reporting, hence employees are not very sure of the reporting lines and sometimes managers are also not very sure as to how to deal with their subordinates as they feel they do not have the requisite authority.

summary: You will enjoy working with DB
advice: good leadership
pros: Deutsche Bank is a slow-growing bank, however, it has its own strategy to keep the strong market and financial positions in the market. you will enjoy  and learn something from working inside. Meanwhile, the working environment is quite political, if you want to further develop you personal skills and control capabilities, DB is a place you should go for. The key point is that you need to speak out and be independent thinking.
cons: So called " German mind set", very process oriented organization. you should be prepared to spend a lot of time in meetings and different engagements. so, don't let yourself be lost in the busy routine and keep focusing on the valuable measures.

summary: Deutsche Bank experience is a true global banking experience.
advice:
1.) Should look at providing better career opportunities to employees globally.
2.) Huge amount of segmentation in business processes has its disadvantages which can be lessened by more appropriate structuring based on business performance.
pros:
1.) Global presence of the bank provides multiple opportunities for qualified individuals.
2.) Great opportunities to learn and great place to start your career.
3.) A professionally managed work environment.
4).) Good performance management system.
cons:
1.) Some amount of bureaucratic behavior is evident in administration.
2.) Organizational policies in developing countries does not match those in developed nations.
3.) Global career opportunities are limited to developed nations.Job opportunities in developed nations are not accessible/available for international employees from less developed nations.

summary: Challenging projects and interesting technology slowed by bureaucracy and politics.
advice:
Further reduce bonus pay tied to "getting it out" by the end of the year. Focus instead on defect rates and production lifecycles as these are more critical and will tie management's decisions to proper SDLC.
Be more stable at the top. We've seen so many heads come and go it is dizzying.
pros:
Great team atmosphere and focus on worklife balance.
Serious focus on agile and doing projects right.
Lots of OSS in use.
Challenging projects with notable impacts.
cons:
Antiquated technology (i.e. Win XP, IE)
Bureaucracy and resources are the hardest part of any IT project.
Politics of higher ups often subverts otherwise logical implementations, dilating project rollouts.

advice: Create more effective hiring standards. Seems that current policy is a roll of the dice with qualified candidates being booted and unqualified candidates being let in.
pros: Money, Money, Money  there can be a lot of money. Great people, and an exhilirating work environment. Would probably say that the bank is better than the competition in all respects: diversity, decent work/life balance for the S&Ts and even sometimes the IBers. transparency with management.
cons: difficult to move up and get foot in the door. There can be some subjectivity in the review process as elsewhere, but the downsides are significantly lower at DB. It can also be beureacratic at times with processes stifling business activity given the size of the bank.

summary: Looks Very Good From Outside Only
advice: Success depends on how you empower people. Managers create atmosphere for success. Remove personal agends of managers for the success of center.
pros: Great Company for benefits. Global company so get to colloborate with employees from various countries. Opportunity to learn from a global prespective.
cons: Missing strong mid level managers. Hiring process can be based on who can recommend their own candidates and not completely on talent or professional background. One can get hired if you know the right people. Preference given mainly to local workforce only. Work experience is based on what team or domain you end up working with. Some teams are really great and some teams not so great.

summary: IT: Very good with some natural drawbacks of a huge company
advice: Be more persistent in transformations
pros:
Speaking about Investment Banking IT (software development) only.
+ Good balance between innovation opportunity and proven solutions for the sake of stability
+ People professionalism
+ Attitude: almost always open, friendly, productive, result-oriented. Even if conflicts appear, it usually happens due to everyone's with to make the best they can but different ways.
+ Internal mobility opportunities. Both geografical and professional
cons:
A few drawbacks natural for a huge organization:
- Some good initiatives, changes may take ages to happen
- 'Global change' initiatives happen often, but come to result... let's say less often
- Sometimes too long management hierarchy make extra barriers
+ But there is always a way to overcome, if you really wish.

advice: Addressing the cons.  Perhaps consider offering strategies that will offer more growth.
pros: Mid-level professionals are quite talented and amicable.  Generally a stable place to work.  New management in Germany seems to be aware of many issues that have hurt the company in the past 5-6 years and may address some of the cons below.
cons: Poorly integrated IT systems.  US management is not given bottom line accountability and poor managers are rarely fired.  Heavy bureaucracy in Germany sometimes prevents things from moving forward elsewhere.  All this has resulted in missed opportunities.  Mid-level employees receive critiques from above and colleagues, but those above do not always receive feed back. Strong focus on fixed income could impact profitability.

advice: Help the bank reward employees earlier than is policy. Promote worthy candidates earlier. Position and pay on more than just years of experience.
pros: Base salary can be low but bonus can be really good.  The bank owns large systems and provides copious opportunities to learn and grow. The types of problems a big bank faces are numerous and always challenging.
cons: Poor hiring practices. Deadlines are everywhere due to regulations. London calls all the shots.  If you're not from London, growth potential is limited. US offices are shadowed greatly by the larger hub offices. Employees don't stay long.

advice: There should be a dept that supports and maintains the "administratives" and not take for granted that we'll always be there. Why are there no positions that can be aspired to? Senior admins have a solid intuitiveness about clients (and their assts) as well as qualifications that aren't nurtured.
pros: When this was Bankers Trust it was a great place to work. After "acquisition"  emphasis was placed squarely on the the managers to make money (which isn't a bad thing) but the way they went about it was wrong.
cons: No effort is made for the non-officer ranks. What you start at -- is generally what you end up as! The "team spirit" was replaced to a "us vs. them" mentality.

summary: Global bank with opportunity to work in diverse business areas
advice: Have to focus on retaining key SMEs in technology and product. Too much internal reorganization. Have to be lean to have focused IT delivery and mature products.
pros: Stable job environment. Lots of mobility options. Opportunities to work on new technology areas. Very good HR processes. Lot of communication from senior management through various forums and internal blogs. Opportunity to work with virtual teams spread across globe.
cons: Stagnant career growth(vertical/compensation) if planning to stay at same location. Too much  senior management overhead. Very difficulty to show results due to long and globally distributed management hierarchy. Performance bonus not typically linked to immediate achievements but more to business line and years with bank.

summary: Started hopeful.  Good in parts.  Mostly disorganized, unsettled and political
advice: The other advice was correct.  Work out what you are.  Protect the few good people, modify the mass of middle managers doing nothing.  If it is a technology place, hire technologists.  If the bank doesn't want the center then close it down and or downsize to the size of effective people left..  Do it fast as they will be leaving soon..
pros:
Being a bulge bracket investment bank in an area evolved for technology and pharm companies means it pays far more than the local area.  There has been some progress where certain applications are now led from the center, but the majority is still "augmentation" with NYC and London calling the shots.  

If you like constant change, then this is the place for you.  Frequent reshuffles and changes in leadership happen, so you could see this as an opportunity if you can stick it out.   Deutsche Bank is undergoing a large scale refactoring akin to the Final Solution, jobs are being created in low-cost centers like Cary, so this creates opportunity.  Promotion is possible - Keep your eyes open and turn up then you will get promoted and receive a fat bonus

It is undergoing some changes to the building, the environment is spacious with lots of walls to put post-it notes on.  There is now more meeting rooms than people - which is good.

Lots of communication from senior managers at the beginning and end of year.

A great choice of food trucks for lunch.
cons:
Cary does "BAU" and stuff that is either not difficult or interesting enough for London to want it.  It is not a "Technology Center" or a "center of excellence" it's just cheaper than working in London and we get the work when London is downsized.

The CTC, as it is now known, underwent significant growth in 2013, then is retracting again in 2014 with a hire-freeze and mass firing.  As the other reviewer mention its is a flailing investment bank and it has recently woke up and realized it has too many people and it is not making enough money to keep them.  Don't worry though, if you can code it will be a long way to get to you.

Little communication from senior managers outside of the beginning and end of year.

Forced ranking.

The hiring process is bad... and you wondered why you stuck it out.  The recruitment team were often to blame but the HR team must accept the majority.  Escalate and make enough noise, then HR wakes up - but why then?  Most of us need jobs for our families.  Make sure you are financially stable and able to take the time out to be on boarded otherwise you will find it V. STRESSFUL.

Agile adoption has become comical.  Even if we wanted it; the external bank thinks it is developer jumbo that can be overridden if they shout loud enough.  They let the agile coaches go, so our walls are full of stagnant yellow notes, toolboxes of avatars and broken dreams.  The place is awash with QA engineers, Scrum Masters and Technical Program Managers.  Lots of managers.  Pretty much everyone apart from coders.

Our town halls are always long and contains announcements about tools.  We have never seen the tools.

Did I mention the politics?  It is sickening.  No matter how much they pay the sugar I still have a bad taste.

advice: Management should not be afraid to grant younger people more responsibilities and possibly the responsibility over a team of older people. Often younger people have better understanding of financial markets, brighter academic backgrounds and a clearer vision of where the business ought to go
pros: Young working environment that allows for a good work/private life balance. Management is very sensible to individual needs and supporting especially with junior colleagues.
cons: Tedious job, range of products is very limited compared to the entire DB potential, in some circumstances the management does not give the idea of being competent in specific areas. Promotions seem to be awarded based on age, merit is somewhat less relevant. Bonuses have only recently pushed up to market average.

advice: With the exception of John Cryan, Deutsche Bank is woefully mismanaged from the top.
pros: Interesting and challenging work; great clients; broad global reach.   Despite Deutsche Bank's deep-rooted issues, pockets of strength remain among its rank and file.
cons: Horribly managed, awful morale, weak compensation and benefits, underperforming equity, antiquated IT, little to no perks.  Deutsche Bank's legacy ethical and legal issues continue to impair the company in nearly every aspect.  The good work of many employees has long been marred by illegal and unethical acts in a way that sr management has been resolve.  As a result, DB is uncompetitive from both an employee and customer standpoint.

summary: Very good job learning about payments.
advice: Maybe be a little more lenient with hitting your case targets for the day.
pros: Learning about payments on a daily basis, further developing skills on internal systems, working as part of a team, nice environment, friendly staff, nice managers,
cons: From my own experience. I was on the German team so some systems were in German language and also some swift messages are in German. Not ideal when you don't speak German but we used google translate and some internal German templates to respond to swifts etc. Not being able to fully understand the swift messages can slow you down in regards to meeting your stats. Apart from that not many cons.

advice: Try not to use vendors for IT development, especially for critical apps. Doing things internally reduces admin overhead tenfold and brings other significant benefits.
pros: Competitive salary, good med insurance, other benefits. Great corporate culture, nice office building, generally it's not hard to find interesting assignments or opportunities. You have to try quite hard to get a promotion, but personally I'm okay with that. You definitely don't need to work crazy hours for an advancement -- can be done in 40-50 hours weeks, if you really put your mind to it.
cons: Some processes are very formal thus, for instance, it takes a lot of time and effort to allocate any resource on a project

advice: Your employees ignore what you say but attend to what you do. Act accordingly.
pros: The Cary, North Carolina physical plant is very nice. It is located right next to the Black Creek Greenway, a pleasant afternoon walk. Promised future renovations include a cafeteria and gym.
cons: They never do things right the first time. Middle management seems incapable of learning from its many failures. Senior management encourages middle management to blame subordinates instead of taking responsibility. The pervasive culture of blame means people spend more time and effort finger-pointing than actually doing work.

advice: You have to buy quality otherwise you should be prepared that it will only attract fresh graduates or low skilled workforce from emerging countries who will leave as soon as a better offer comes. Sustainibility in the risk area is key and this concept does not exist at DB.
pros: Scope of covered areas, really the top of the profession. Insight to the full operation of a universal bank. Some very well educated and respectful colleagues with the necessary drive.
cons:
- Salary way below the sectoral standard in the light of the experience needed for the job
- Life-Work balance non existant
- Annoyingly unserious career plans and compensation packages
- Many mistakes and delays due to bureaucracy

advice: You have to figure out a better way to motivate and keep employees, almost all of my previous colleagues who were decent programmers left for better salaries or opportunities
pros: Initial salary was competitive, colleagues were not the typical neckbearded programmers, there were some opportunities to work with some newer technologies, development work was decent

summary: Some glimmers of light, though Cary leadership leave little to be desired.
advice:
This advice is to the management above Cary: Please come and review the Cary management.  Please read the other Glassdoor reviews.  Please, please, help.  There are souls worth saving.
Tech leaders should be technologists.
pros:
Contrary to the doom and gloom the media conveys about Deutsche Bank, the wider bank (external of the Cary office) is surprisingly interesting and there are a few nuggets of optimism.  With the recent senior management changes at board level, there are some glimmers of sense as the much needed rationalisation has happened in abundance - hopefully the target will soon be on the local Cary Director "leadership" as there is plenty of dead wood to strip there.

The working area is ok.  Somewhat like a call center instead of a development environment, which is kinda ok as not a huge amount of real development happens here.  Elbow room is in short supply, but this is compensated by the comedy of the center wide town halls which are a real hoot!
Deutsche Bank benefits are great.  Free holiday, pension, health-care and the work-life-balance of what is essentially an easy life make this an opportunity that is hard to overlook for anyone.  Second jobbing is entirely possible.
Bonuses went the way of the dodo a few years back and this resulted in a brain drain that made us a popular invite for any quiz-based social.  Gallows humor is common-place, which is a real positive, especially with the yearly cycle of musical chairs where we are often dumb-founded by the same near-misses year after year.
In the absence of old-style banking compensation, the balance of few promotions has swung to "promote anyone" this is good for the long-termers as there must be some corrections to be made, however it's a "Con" too (I'll describe below).
cons:
The nuggets of good I referred to as a positive are sadly not evident in Cary.  There are nuggets, just a different type, and this would nicely describe the local directorship.  The ego amongst the non-contributor population is often breathtaking.  Lots of references to "my guys", but little loyalty come compensation distribution and standing up to their higher achieving counterparts in the Financial Centers.
In reference to the "promote anyone" mentality, the quality requirement bar has dropped significantly.    Being a senior leader at Deutsche Bank use to really mean something with the MDs and Directors being some of the best in the game, now I would suggest they are operating at a minus one, as-in, MDs are the old Directors, Directors -> VPs and so-on.  Self awarding titles such as "President" for technology management with no apparent technology capability is demotivating for anyone with a technology aspiration.

advice: Paradigm shift. Doing the same thing and expecting the same result. Learn from American banks. Technology drives business.

The technologies are so archaic which in turn hurts the business. Rapidly losing good talent and bringing in mediocre talent to replace and at a cheaper rate. Compensation 
 is sub par compared to other financial service firms, with no raise and a bonus that should not even be called a bonus.
